title.zh: 卷四百七十五 列傳第二百三十四 叛臣上 張邦昌 劉豫 苗傅劉正彥 杜充 吳曦
title.en: Volume 475 Biographies 234: Rebellious Officials 1: Zhang Bangchang, Liu Yu, Miao Fuliuzhengyan, Du Chong, Wu Xi
title.raw: 卷四百七十五 列傳第二百三十四 叛臣上 張邦昌 劉豫 苗傅劉正彥 杜充 吳曦 Volume 475 Biographies 234: Rebellious Officials 1: Zhang Bangchang, Liu Yu, Miao Fuliuzhengyan, Du Chong, Wu Xi

sentences.zh: 一三七八九页：張邦昌 劉豫 苗傅劉正彥附 杜充 吳曦

translations.literal: Pages 13789: Zhang Bangchang, Liu Yu, Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan (appendix), Du Chong, Wu Xi
translations.idiomatic: Pages 13789: Zhang Bangchang, Liu Yu, Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan (with appendix), Du Chong, and Wu Xi

sentences.zh: 宋失其政，金人乘之，俘其人民，遷其寶器，效遼故事，立其臣爲君，冠屨易位，莫甚斯時。

translations.literal: The Song lost proper governance; the Jurchens seized the opportunity, captured its people, and removed its precious vessels. Following the Liao precedent, they installed a Song minister as ruler. Crown and sandals exchanged places—never was the inversion more extreme than in this age.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song forfeited good government, the Jurchens pressed their advantage: they took the people captive, carried off the imperial treasures, and, imitating what the Liao had done before, set up a Song subject as king. Ruler and subject traded places as never before.

sentences.zh: 高宗南渡，國勢弗振，悍僕狂奴，欺主衰敗，易動於惡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong crossed south, national strength did not recover. Fierce servants and reckless underlings, seeing their lord in decline, were easily moved to evil.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozong fled south across the Yangtze, the dynasty never regained its strength. Bold servants and reckless retainers, finding their master enfeebled, were quick to turn to treachery.

sentences.zh: 兵雖凶器，尤忌殘忍，將用忍人，先無仁心，視背君親猶反掌耳。

translations.literal: Though arms are instruments of violence, cruelty is especially to be feared. To employ a ruthless man as general—one who lacks humaneness beforehand—is to treat betrayal of sovereign and kin as no more than turning one's palm.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons are brutal by nature, but cruelty in their use is doubly dangerous. A commander chosen for his ruthlessness, lacking humaneness from the start, will betray sovereign and kin as readily as he turns his hand.

sentences.zh: 世將之子使握重兵，居之阨塞之地，豈非召亂之道乎？

translations.literal: To let the son of a hereditary general hold heavy troops and station him in a strategic pass—is this not a way to summon disorder?
translations.idiomatic: To place the heir of a military house in command of a great army at a strategic choke point—is that not inviting rebellion?

sentences.zh: 大義昭明，旋踵殄滅，蓋天道也。

translations.literal: When great righteousness is made clear, swift annihilation follows—such is Heaven's way.
translations.idiomatic: When the moral order stands plain, traitors are destroyed in short order—such is the way of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 扶綱常，遏亂略，作《叛臣傳》。

translations.literal: To uphold the constants of propriety and restrain the schemes of disorder, the 'Biographies of Rebellious Ministers' was composed.
translations.idiomatic: To uphold moral order and check the designs of rebels, this 'Biographies of Rebellious Ministers' was written.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌

translations.literal: Zhang Bangchang
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bangchang

sentences.zh: 張邦昌，字子能，永靜軍東光人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Bangchang, courtesy name Zineng, was a native of Dongguang in Yongjing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bangchang, styled Zineng, came from Dongguang in Yongjing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，累官大司成，以訓導失職，貶提舉崇福宮，知光、汝二州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and rose through offices to Grand Director of Education. For failure in instruction and guidance he was demoted to commissioner of Chongfu Palace and served as prefect of Guang and Ru prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi graduate, he rose to Grand Director of Education, but was demoted for dereliction in teaching and made commissioner of Chongfu Palace before serving as prefect of Guang and Ru.

sentences.zh: 政和末，由知洪州改禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenghe era, he moved from prefect of Hongzhou to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhenghe reign, he was transferred from Hongzhou prefect to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 首請取崇寧、大觀以來瑞應尤殊者增製旗物，從之。

translations.literal: He was first to request that the most extraordinary auspicious signs since Chongning and Daguan be used to add new banners and regalia; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He first proposed commissioning new banners and ceremonial objects from the most remarkable omens recorded since Chongning and Daguan, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 宣和元年，除尚書右丞，轉左丞，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanhe he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, then Left Vice Director, then promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 1 he became Right Vice Director of State Affairs, then Left Vice Director, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 欽宗即位，拜少宰。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong acceded, Bangchang was appointed Junior Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qinzong took the throne, Bangchang was made Junior Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 金人犯京師，朝廷議割三鎮，俾康王及邦昌爲質于金以求成。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens attacked the capital, the court debated ceding the Three Circuits and sending the Prince of Kang and Bangchang as hostages to the Jin to seek peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens besieged the capital, the court considered ceding the Three Circuits and sending the Prince of Kang and Bangchang to the Jin as hostages in exchange for peace.

sentences.zh: 會姚平仲夜斫金人營，斡離不怒責邦昌，邦昌對以非出朝廷意。

translations.literal: When Yao Pingzhong raided the Jin camp by night, Wanyan Zonghan angrily rebuked Bangchang, who replied that this was not the court's intent.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Pingzhong's night attack on the Jin camp, Wanyan Zonghan rebuked Bangchang in anger; Bangchang answered that the court had not authorized it.

sentences.zh: 俄進太宰兼門下侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly he was promoted to Grand Chancellor concurrent with Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Grand Chancellor while retaining the post of Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 既而康王還，金人復質肅王以行，仍命邦昌爲河北路割地使。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Kang returned, the Jin again took the Prince of Su as hostage and ordered Bangchang to serve as commissioner for ceding territory in Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Kang came back, the Jin took the Prince of Su hostage instead and appointed Bangchang commissioner for the cession of Hebei territory.

sentences.zh: 初，邦昌力主和議，不意身自爲質，及行，乃要欽宗署御批無變割地議，不許；

translations.literal: At first Bangchang had strongly advocated peace; he had not expected to become a hostage himself. When he set out, he demanded that Qinzong sign an imperial rescript pledging no change to the cession policy; this was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang had long pushed for peace talks and never imagined he would become a hostage himself. Before departing he asked Qinzong to sign a rescript forbidding any change to the cession policy; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 又請以璽書付河北，亦不許。

translations.literal: He also asked that an imperial seal document be sent to Hebei; this too was denied.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that an imperial sealed edict be delivered to Hebei, but that was denied as well.

sentences.zh: 時粘罕兵又來侵，上書者攻邦昌私敵，社稷之賊也。

translations.literal: At that time Nianhan's army invaded again; memorialists attacked Bangchang as secretly aiding the enemy, a traitor to the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: When Nianhan's forces invaded again, memorialists denounced Bangchang as a secret friend of the enemy and a traitor to the realm.

sentences.zh: 遂黜邦昌爲觀文殿大學士、中太一宮使，罷割地議。

translations.literal: Bangchang was then demoted to Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature and commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace, and the cession talks were halted.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang was stripped of power, made Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature and commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace, and the cession policy was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 其冬，金人陷京師，帝再出郊，留青城。

translations.literal: That winter the Jin took the capital; the emperor again went out to the suburbs and remained at Qingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Jin captured the capital; the emperor went out to the suburbs a second time and stayed at Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 明年春，吳開、莫儔自金營持文書來，令推異姓堪爲人主者從軍前備禮冊命。

translations.literal: The next spring Wu Kai and Mo Chou came from the Jin camp with documents ordering that a man of another surname fit to be ruler be chosen and sent to the army front to prepare the ritual investiture.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Wu Kai and Mo Chou arrived from the Jin camp with orders to nominate a worthy man of non-Zhao surname and send him to the Jin headquarters to receive investiture.

sentences.zh: 留守孫傅等不奉命，表請立趙氏。

translations.literal: The acting prefect Sun Fu and others refused the order and memorialized asking that a member of the Zhao house be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Acting prefect Sun Fu and others defied the order and petitioned to enthrone a Zhao clansman.

sentences.zh: 金人怒，復遣開、儔促之，劫傅等召百官雜議。

translations.literal: The Jin were enraged and again sent Kai and Chou to press the matter, coercing Fu and the rest to summon the officials for a general discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the Jin sent Kai and Chou back to hurry matters along and forced Fu and his colleagues to convene the officials for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 衆莫敢出聲，相視久之，計無所出，乃曰：「今日當勉強應命，舉在軍前者一人。」

translations.literal: No one dared speak; they looked at one another a long time with no plan, and at last said: 'Today we must reluctantly obey and nominate one man already at the army front.'
translations.idiomatic: No one dared speak. After a long silence they could find no way out and said, 'We must reluctantly comply today and nominate someone already at the Jin camp.'

sentences.zh: 適尚書員外郎宋齊愈至自外，衆問金人意所主，齊愈書「張邦昌」三字示之，遂定議，以邦昌治國事。

translations.literal: Just then Song Qiyu, an outer-office attache of the Secretariat, arrived from outside. The assembly asked whom the Jin favored; Qiyu wrote the three characters 'Zhang Bangchang' and showed them. The decision was fixed, and Bangchang was put in charge of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Song Qiyu, an outer-office attache of the Secretariat, came in from outside. When asked whom the Jin preferred, he wrote 'Zhang Bangchang' and showed it to the assembly. The choice was settled, and Bangchang was placed in charge of government.

sentences.zh: 孫傅、張叔夜不署狀，金人執之置軍中。

translations.literal: Sun Fu and Zhang Shuye refused to sign the petition; the Jin seized them and held them in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu and Zhang Shuye refused to sign; the Jin arrested them and kept them in the army camp.

sentences.zh: 王時雍時爲留守，再集百官詣秘書省，至即閉省門，以兵環之，俾範瓊諭衆以立邦昌，衆意唯唯。

translations.literal: Wang Shiyong was then acting prefect. He again gathered the officials at the Secretariat; on arrival the gates were shut and troops surrounded them. Fan Qiong was made to announce to the assembly the enthronement of Bangchang; the crowd murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiyong, then acting prefect, assembled the officials again at the Secretariat. As soon as they arrived the gates were shut and soldiers ringed the building. Fan Qiong was told to announce Bangchang's enthronement; the officials murmured reluctant agreement.

sentences.zh: 有太學生難之，瓊恐沮衆，厲聲折之，遣歸學舍。

translations.literal: A student of the Imperial Academy objected; fearing this would discourage the crowd, Qiong rebuked him sharply and sent him back to the dormitory.
translations.idiomatic: When a student of the Imperial Academy objected, Qiong, fearing he would dampen the assembly's resolve, shouted him down and sent him back to the dormitory.

sentences.zh: 時雍先署狀，以率百官。

translations.literal: Shiyong signed the petition first to lead the other officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong signed first to set an example for the rest.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞秦檜不書，抗言請立趙氏宗室，且言邦昌當上皇時，專事宴遊，党附權奸，蠹國亂政，社稷傾危實由邦昌。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Qin Hui refused to sign and spoke out, asking that a Zhao clansman be enthroned. He said that when Bangchang served under the Retired Emperor he devoted himself to feasting and pleasure, clung to powerful villains, harmed the state and disrupted government, and that the peril to the altars of state was truly due to Bangchang.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Qin Hui would not sign. He protested that a Zhao prince should be enthroned, and declared that under the Retired Emperor Bangchang had done nothing but feast, attached himself to corrupt power-holders, ruined the state, and brought the dynasty to the brink of collapse.

sentences.zh: 金人怒，執檜。

translations.literal: The Jin were enraged and seized Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin were furious and arrested Hui.

sentences.zh: 開、儔持狀赴軍前。

translations.literal: Kai and Chou carried the petition to the army front.
translations.idiomatic: Kai and Chou took the signed petition to the Jin camp.

sentences.zh: 邦昌入居尚書省，金人趣勸進，邦昌始欲引決，或曰：「相公不前死城外，今欲塗炭一城耶？」

translations.literal: Bangchang moved into the Secretariat. The Jin urged him to accept the throne. At first he wished to take his own life, but someone said: 'My lord, you would not die outside the walls before; will you now bring ruin on a whole city?'
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang took up residence in the Secretariat. The Jin pressed him to accept the throne. He first meant to kill himself, but someone said, 'You would not die outside the walls when you had the chance—will you now condemn the whole city?'

sentences.zh: 適金人奉冊寶至，邦昌北向拜舞受冊，即偽位，僭號大楚，擬都金陵。

translations.literal: Just then the Jin presented the investiture documents and regalia. Bangchang faced north, bowed and danced in acceptance, and took the usurped throne, styling his state Great Chu and planning to make Jinling the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Jin delivered the investiture regalia. Bangchang faced north, performed the full obeisance, and accepted the throne. He proclaimed the state Great Chu and planned to establish his capital at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 遂升文德殿，設位御床西受賀，遣閤門傳令勿拜，時雍率百官遽拜，邦昌但東面拱立。

translations.literal: He then ascended the Hall of Literary Virtue, set his seat west of the imperial couch to receive congratulations, and sent the Gate Office to transmit an order that no bowing was required. Shiyong led the officials in hasty bows while Bangchang merely stood facing east with hands clasped.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hall of Literary Virtue, took a seat west of the imperial couch to receive congratulations, and sent the Gate Office to say that no bowing was needed. Shiyong led the officials in hurried bows while Bangchang only stood facing east with clasped hands.

sentences.zh: 外統制官、宣贊舍人吳革恥屈節異姓，首率內親事官數百人，皆先殺其妻孥，焚所居，謀舉義金水門外。

translations.literal: Wu Ge, an outer controller and Palace Announcement Attendant, ashamed to submit to a ruler of another surname, was first to lead several hundred inner-service officers. Each first killed wife and children, burned his dwelling, and planned to raise arms outside the Jinshui Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ge, an outer controller and Palace Announcement Attendant, scorned bowing to a usurper. He led several hundred inner-service officers who first killed their wives and children, burned their homes, and planned an uprising outside the Jinshui Gate.

sentences.zh: 範瓊詐與合謀，令悉棄兵仗，乃從後襲殺百餘人，捕革並其子皆殺之，又擒斬十餘人。

translations.literal: Fan Qiong feigned joining the plot and ordered them all to lay down arms, then attacked from behind and killed more than a hundred. Ge and his sons were captured and executed, and more than ten others were seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Qiong pretended to join the conspiracy and told them to lay down their weapons, then attacked from the rear and killed more than a hundred. Ge and his sons were captured and killed, along with more than ten others.

sentences.zh: 是日，風霾，日暈無光。

translations.literal: That day there was wind and haze; the sun had a halo and no brightness.
translations.idiomatic: That day wind and dust filled the air; the sun was ringed with haze and gave no light.

sentences.zh: 百官慘沮，邦昌亦變色。

translations.literal: The officials were wretched and downcast; Bangchang too changed color.
translations.idiomatic: The officials looked stricken; Bangchang's face fell as well.

sentences.zh: 唯時雍、開、儔、瓊等欣然鼓舞，若以爲有佐命功雲。

translations.literal: Only Shiyong, Kai, Chou, Qiong, and the like rejoiced and exulted, as though they had merit in aiding the founding of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shiyong, Kai, Chou, Qiong, and their ilk rejoiced, as if they had earned merit in founding a new dynasty.

sentences.zh: 即以時雍權知樞密院事領尚書省，開權同知樞密院事，儔權簽書樞密院事，呂好問權領門下省，徐秉哲權領中書省。

translations.literal: Shiyong was made acting head of the Bureau of Military Affairs while directing the Secretariat; Kai acting associate director of military affairs; Chou acting signatory of military affairs; Lü Haowen acting head of the Chancellery; Xu Bingzhe acting head of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong was made acting head of the Bureau of Military Affairs and the Secretariat; Kai acting associate director of military affairs; Chou acting signatory; Lü Haowen acting head of the Chancellery; and Xu Bingzhe acting head of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 下令曰：「比緣朝廷多故，百官有司皆失其職。

translations.literal: An order was issued: 'Recently, because the court has faced many crises, officials at every level have neglected their duties.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: 'Because the court has been in turmoil, officials at every level have neglected their duties.

sentences.zh: 自今各遵法度，御史台覺察以聞。」

translations.literal: From now on each shall observe the laws; the Censorate shall investigate and report.'
translations.idiomatic: From now on all must observe the law; the Censorate will investigate and report violations.'

sentences.zh: 見百官稱「予」，手詔曰「手書」。

translations.literal: In addressing officials he called himself 'I'; imperial autographs were styled 'handwriting.'
translations.idiomatic: When meeting officials he called himself 'I,' and his personal edicts were titled 'handwriting' rather than imperial rescripts.

sentences.zh: 獨時雍每言事邦昌前，輒稱「臣啟陛下」，邦昌斥之；

translations.literal: Only Shiyong, whenever he spoke before Bangchang, would say 'Your servant reports to Your Majesty'; Bangchang rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shiyong, whenever he addressed Bangchang, would say 'Your servant reports to Your Majesty,' and Bangchang rebuked him for it.

sentences.zh: 勸邦昌坐紫宸、垂拱殿，呂好問爭之，乃止。

translations.literal: They urged Bangchang to sit in the Purple Forbidden and Bowing Hall; Lü Haowen objected, and the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Bangchang to take his seat in the Purple Forbidden and Bowing Hall; Lü Haowen protested, and the idea was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 邦昌以嗣位之初，宜推恩四方，以道阻先赦京城，選郎官爲四方密諭使。

translations.literal: Bangchang thought that at the beginning of his succession he should extend grace to the four quarters; because roads were blocked he first pardoned the capital region and chose court gentlemen as secret envoys to the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of his reign Bangchang wished to extend clemency throughout the realm; because travel was blocked he first proclaimed an amnesty in the capital and appointed court gentlemen as secret envoys to the provinces.

sentences.zh: 金人將退師，邦昌詣金營祖別，服柘袍，張紅蓋，所過設香案，起居悉如常儀，時雍、秉哲、開、儔皆從行，士庶觀者無不感愴。

translations.literal: When the Jin were about to withdraw, Bangchang went to their camp to offer a farewell feast. He wore a russet robe and raised a red canopy; incense tables were set along the route and all courtesies were as in normal ritual. Shiyong, Bingzhe, Kai, and Chou all followed. Commoners who watched were moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: As the Jin prepared to withdraw, Bangchang went to their camp for a farewell banquet. He wore a russet robe under a red canopy; incense tables lined his path and every courtesy was observed as in ordinary court ritual. Shiyong, Bingzhe, Kai, and Chou accompanied him. The crowds who watched were overcome with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 二帝北遷，邦昌率百官遙辭于南薰門，衆慟哭，有僕絕者。

translations.literal: When the two emperors were moved north, Bangchang led the officials in a distant farewell at the Southern Fragrance Gate. The crowd wept bitterly; some collapsed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the two emperors were taken north, Bangchang led the officials in a distant farewell at the Southern Fragrance Gate. The assembly wept aloud; some fainted from grief.

sentences.zh: 金師既還，邦昌降手書赦天下。

translations.literal: After the Jin army had returned, Bangchang issued a personal edict pardoning all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jin army had withdrawn, Bangchang issued a personal edict granting a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 呂好問謂邦昌曰：「人情歸公者、劫于金人之威耳，金人既去，能復有今日乎？

translations.literal: Lü Haowen said to Bangchang: 'Those who follow you do so only under Jin coercion. Once the Jin are gone, can you still hold today?
translations.idiomatic: Lü Haowen told Bangchang, 'The people follow you only because the Jin forced them to. Once the Jin are gone, can you really keep what you have today?

sentences.zh: 康王居外久，衆所歸心，曷不推戴之？」

translations.literal: The Prince of Kang has long been abroad and is where hearts turn—why not support him?'
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Kang has been away a long time and commands everyone's loyalty—why not enthrone him?'

sentences.zh: 又謂曰：「爲今計者，當迎元祐皇后，請康王早正大位，庶獲保全。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'For the present plan, you should welcome the Yuanyou Empress Dowager and ask the Prince of Kang to take the throne early, so that you may perhaps preserve yourself.'
translations.idiomatic: He added, 'The wise course now is to welcome the Yuanyou Empress Dowager and urge the Prince of Kang to take the throne at once—only then might you save yourself.'

sentences.zh: 監察御史馬伸亦請奉迎康王。

translations.literal: Supervising censor Ma Shen also petitioned to welcome the Prince of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor Ma Shen likewise petitioned to welcome the Prince of Kang.

sentences.zh: 邦昌從之。

translations.literal: Bangchang followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang agreed.

sentences.zh: 王時雍曰：「夫騎虎者勢不得下，所宜熟慮，他日噬臍，悔無及已。」

translations.literal: Wang Shiyong said: 'One who rides a tiger cannot easily dismount. You should think carefully; later you may bite your navel in regret when it is too late.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiyong said, 'A man who rides a tiger cannot climb down easily. Think this through carefully—one day you may bite your navel in regret when it is too late.'

sentences.zh: 徐秉哲從旁贊之，邦昌弗聽，乃冊元祐皇后曰宋太后，入御延福宮。

translations.literal: Xu Bingzhe seconded him from the side, but Bangchang would not listen. He then invested the Yuanyou Empress Dowager as Song Empress Dowager and installed her in Yanfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bingzhe chimed in from the side, but Bangchang would not listen. He invested the Yuanyou Empress Dowager as Song Empress Dowager and installed her in Yanfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 遣蔣師愈齎書于康王自陳：「所以勉循金人推戴者，欲權宜一時以紓國難也，敢有他乎？」

translations.literal: He sent Jiang Shiyu with a letter to the Prince of Kang explaining: 'The reason I reluctantly followed the Jin in enthroning me was to make a temporary expedient to ease the national crisis—would I dare have any other intent?'
translations.idiomatic: He sent Jiang Shiyu with a letter to the Prince of Kang explaining that he had only reluctantly accepted the Jin nomination as a temporary expedient to ease the national crisis and had no other ambition.

sentences.zh: 王詢師愈等，具知所由，乃報書邦昌。

translations.literal: The prince questioned Shiyu and the rest and learned the full story, then sent a reply to Bangchang.
translations.idiomatic: The prince questioned Shiyu and learned the full story, then wrote back to Bangchang.

sentences.zh: 邦昌尋遣謝克家獻大宋受命寶，復降手書請元祐皇后垂簾聽政，以俟復辟。

translations.literal: Bangchang soon sent Xie Kejia to present the Great Song Seal of Mandate and again issued a personal edict asking the Yuanyou Empress Dowager to rule from behind the curtain until the throne was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang soon sent Xie Kejia to present the Great Song Seal of Mandate and issued another personal edict asking the Yuanyou Empress Dowager to rule from behind the curtain until the rightful sovereign returned.

sentences.zh: 書既下，中外大說。

translations.literal: Once the edict was issued, court and country rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, the court and the realm rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 太后始御內東門小殿，垂簾聽政。

translations.literal: The empress dowager first took the small hall at the Inner Eastern Gate and ruled from behind the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager took up audience in the small hall at the Inner Eastern Gate and began ruling from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 邦昌乙太宰退處內東門資善堂。

translations.literal: Bangchang left the post of Grand Chancellor and retired to the Hall for Cultivating Virtue at the Inner Eastern Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang resigned as Grand Chancellor and withdrew to the Hall for Cultivating Virtue at the Inner Eastern Gate.

sentences.zh: 尋遣使奉乘輿服御物至南京，既而邦昌亦至，伏地慟哭請死，王撫慰之。

translations.literal: Soon envoys were sent bearing the imperial carriage, robes, and regalia to Nanjing. Bangchang also came, prostrated himself, wept, and begged for death; the prince comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon sent envoys bearing the imperial carriage, robes, and regalia to Nanjing. Bangchang followed, threw himself to the ground weeping, and begged for death; the prince comforted him.

sentences.zh: 王即皇帝位，相李綱，徙邦昌太保、奉國軍節度使，封同安郡王。

translations.literal: The prince took the throne and made Li Gang his chief minister. Bangchang was moved to Grand Mentor and military commissioner of Fengguo Army, and enfeoffed as Prince of Tong'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The prince ascended the throne and appointed Li Gang chief minister. Bangchang was made Grand Mentor and military commissioner of the Fengguo Army and enfeoffed as Prince of Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 綱上書極論：「邦昌久典機政，擢冠宰司。

translations.literal: Gang memorialized at length: 'Bangchang long held the reins of power and rose to head the council of state.
translations.idiomatic: Gang memorialized forcefully: 'Bangchang long held the levers of power and rose to the head of government.

sentences.zh: 國破而資之以爲利，君辱而攘之以爲榮。

translations.literal: When the state was broken he profited from it; when his sovereign was shamed he seized glory for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He profited from the nation's ruin and treated his sovereign's humiliation as his own glory.

sentences.zh: 異姓建邦四十餘日，逮金人之既退，方降赦以收恩。

translations.literal: He founded a state of another surname for more than forty days, and only after the Jin had withdrawn did he issue a pardon to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled a usurper state for more than forty days and issued a general amnesty only after the Jin withdrew—to win back goodwill.

sentences.zh: 是宜肆諸市朝，以爲亂臣賊子之戒。」

translations.literal: He should be exposed in the marketplace as a warning to traitorous ministers and rebellious sons.'
translations.idiomatic: He should be executed in public as a warning to every traitor and rebel.'

sentences.zh: 時黃潛善猶左右之。

translations.literal: At the time Huang Qianshan still supported him at court.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Huang Qianshan still spoke in his favor at court.

sentences.zh: 綱又力言：「邦昌已僭逆，豈可留之朝廷，使道路目爲故天子哉？」

translations.literal: Gang again argued forcefully: 'Bangchang has already usurped the throne—how can he be kept at court so that travelers on the road look on him as the former emperor?'
translations.idiomatic: Gang argued again: 'Bangchang has already committed treason. How can we keep him at court and let people on the road treat him as the former emperor?'

sentences.zh: 高宗乃降御批曰：「邦昌僭逆，理合誅夷，原其初心，出於迫脅，可特與免貸，責授昭化軍節度副使、潭州安置。」

translations.literal: Gaozong then issued an imperial rescript: 'Bangchang's usurpation merits execution, but considering his original intent arose from coercion, he is specially spared and demoted to vice military commissioner of Zhaohua Army, to be settled at Tanzhou.'
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong issued a rescript: 'Bangchang's treason deserves death, but since he acted under duress, he is specially spared and demoted to vice military commissioner of the Zhaohua Army, to be settled at Tanzhou.'

sentences.zh: 初，邦昌僭居內庭，華國靖恭夫人李氏數以果實奉邦昌，邦昌亦厚答之。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Bangchang usurped residence in the inner palace, Lady Li of Huaguo Jinggong several times sent him fruit; Bangchang also rewarded her generously.
translations.idiomatic: While Bangchang occupied the inner palace, Lady Li of Huaguo Jinggong often sent him fruit, and he repaid her generously.

sentences.zh: 一夕，邦昌被酒，李氏擁之曰：「大家，事已至此，尚何言？」

translations.literal: One evening Bangchang was drunk. Lady Li embraced him and said: 'My lord, matters have come to this—what more is there to say?'
translations.idiomatic: One night, drunk, Bangchang was embraced by Lady Li, who said, 'My lord, things have gone this far—what is left to say?'

sentences.zh: 因以赭色半臂加邦昌身，掖入福寧殿，夜飾養女陳氏以進。

translations.literal: She then put a russet half-sleeve on Bangchang, supported him into the Hall of Blessings and Tranquility, and that night dressed her foster daughter Chen and presented her to him.
translations.idiomatic: She put a russet half-sleeve on him, led him into the Hall of Blessings and Tranquility, and that night dressed her foster daughter Chen and presented her to him.

sentences.zh: 及邦昌還東府，李氏私送之，語斥乘輿。

translations.literal: When Bangchang returned to the Eastern Residence, Lady Li saw him off in private and spoke contemptuously of the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Bangchang returned to the Eastern Residence, Lady Li saw him off privately and spoke disrespectfully of the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，下李氏獄，詞服。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this, Lady Li was imprisoned; she confessed under interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, Lady Li was imprisoned and confessed under interrogation.

sentences.zh: 詔數邦昌罪，賜死潭州，李氏杖脊配車營務。

translations.literal: An edict enumerated Bangchang's crimes and ordered him to die by imperial grace at Tanzhou. Lady Li was beaten on the back and assigned to carriage service duty.
translations.idiomatic: An edict listed Bangchang's crimes and ordered him to take his own life at Tanzhou. Lady Li was flogged and assigned to menial carriage service.

sentences.zh: 時雍、秉哲、開、儔等先已遠竄，至是，並誅時雍。

translations.literal: Shiyong, Bingzhe, Kai, Chou, and the rest had already been exiled far away; at this time Shiyong was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong, Bingzhe, Kai, Chou, and the others had already been exiled; now Shiyong was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 劉豫，字彥游，景州阜城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yu, courtesy name Yanyou, was a native of Fucheng in Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, styled Yanyou, came from Fucheng in Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世業農，至豫始舉進士，元符中登第。

translations.literal: His family had farmed for generations; Yu was the first to take the jinshi examination and passed in the Yuanfu era.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been farmers for generations; he was the first to sit for the jinshi examination and passed in the Yuanfu era.

sentences.zh: 豫少時無行，嘗盜同舍生白盂、紗衣。

translations.literal: In youth Yu was without proper conduct and once stole a white bowl and gauze garment from a fellow lodger.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was ill-behaved and once stole a white bowl and gauze robe from a roommate.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，召拜殿中侍御史，爲言者所擊，帝不欲發其宿醜，詔勿問。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe he was summoned as palace attendant censor. Critics attacked him, but the emperor did not wish to expose his old disgrace and ordered that the matter not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 2 he was appointed palace attendant censor. Critics attacked him, but the emperor declined to expose his past misconduct and ordered the matter dropped.

sentences.zh: 未幾，豫累章言禮制局事，帝曰：「劉豫河北種田叟，安識禮制？」

translations.literal: Before long Yu repeatedly memorialized on matters of the Bureau of Rites. The emperor said: 'Liu Yu is a Hebei farming fellow—how would he know ritual?'
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yu sent repeated memorials on the Bureau of Rites. The emperor said, 'Liu Yu is a Hebei farmer—what does he know about ritual?'

sentences.zh: 黜豫兩浙察訪。

translations.literal: Yu was demoted to inspector of the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to inspector of the Two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 宣和六年，判國子監，除河北提刑。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuanhe he was made administrator of the Directorate of Education and appointed judicial intendant of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 6 he administered the Directorate of Education and was appointed judicial intendant of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 金人南侵，豫棄官避亂儀真。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens invaded south, Yu abandoned his post and fled the turmoil to Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens invaded the south, Yu abandoned his post and fled to Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 豫善中書侍郎張愨，建炎二年正月，用愨薦除知濟南府。

translations.literal: Yu was on good terms with Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhang Kai. In the first month of the second year of Jianyan, on Kai's recommendation he was appointed prefect of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was friendly with Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhang Kai. In the first month of Jianyan 2, on Kai's recommendation he was appointed prefect of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 時盜起山東，豫不願行，請易東南一郡，執政惡之，不許，豫忿而去。

translations.literal: Bandits had risen in Shandong; Yu did not wish to go and asked to exchange for a southeastern prefecture. The chief ministers disliked this and refused; Yu left in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rising in Shandong. Yu did not want the post and asked for a southeastern prefecture instead. The chief ministers refused, and Yu left in a rage.

sentences.zh: 是冬，金人攻濟南，豫遣子麟出戰，敵縱兵圍之數重，郡倅張柬益兵來援，金人乃解去。

translations.literal: That winter the Jin attacked Jinan. Yu sent his son Lin into battle. The enemy loosened their troops and surrounded them in several rings; vice-prefect Zhang Dong reinforced with troops and the Jin then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Jin attacked Jinan. Yu sent his son Lin to fight. The enemy surrounded them in several rings until vice-prefect Zhang Dong brought reinforcements and the Jin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 因遣人啖豫以利，豫懲前忿，遂畜反謀，殺其將關勝，率百姓降金，百姓不從，豫縋城納款。

translations.literal: They then sent men to entice Yu with profit. Yu, mindful of his earlier grievance, nurtured a plan of rebellion, killed his general Guan Sheng, and tried to lead the people in surrender to the Jin. The people would not follow; Yu was lowered over the wall to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent envoys to tempt him with rewards. Still smarting from his earlier humiliation, Yu plotted treason, killed his general Guan Sheng, and tried to lead the people in surrender. When they refused, he was lowered over the wall to submit to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，兀朮聞高宗渡江，乃徙豫知東平府，充京東西、淮南等路安撫使，節制大名開德府、濮濱博棣德滄等州，以麟知濟南府，界舊河以南，俾豫統之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year, Wuzhu heard that Gaozong had crossed the Yangtze and moved Yu to prefect of Dongping, made him pacification commissioner of Jingdong, Jingxi, Huainan, and other circuits, with control over Daming-Kaifeng, Pu, Bin, Bo, Di, De, Cang, and other prefectures. Lin was made prefect of Jinan. South of the old Yellow River boundary, Yu was put in command.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 3, hearing that Gaozong had crossed the Yangtze, Wuzhu transferred Yu to Dongping prefect and made him pacification commissioner over Jingdong, Jingxi, Huainan, and related circuits, with authority over Daming-Kaifeng, Pu, Bin, Bo, Di, De, Cang, and other prefectures. Lin was made prefect of Jinan. Everything south of the old Yellow River was placed under Yu's command.

sentences.zh: 四年七月丁卯，金人遣大同尹高慶裔、知制誥韓昉册豫爲皇帝，國號大齊，都大名府。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the seventh month of the fourth year, the Jin sent Grand Unity Director Gao Qingyi and Drafting Academician Han Fang to invest Yu as emperor. His state was called Great Qi and its capital was Daming.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao in the seventh month of year 4, the Jin sent Grand Unity Director Gao Qingyi and Drafting Academician Han Fang to invest Yu as emperor. He proclaimed the state Great Qi with its capital at Daming.

sentences.zh: 先是，北京順豫門生瑞禾，濟南漁者得鳣，豫以爲己受命之符，遣麟持重寶賂金左監軍撻辣求僭號。

translations.literal: Earlier, an auspicious grain had grown at the Shunyu Gate of the Northern Capital and a fisherman at Jinan had caught a sturgeon. Yu took these as signs of his mandate and sent Lin with heavy treasures to bribe the Jin Left Military Supervisor Talaha to seek the title of emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an auspicious grain had appeared at the Shunyu Gate in the Northern Capital and a Jinan fisherman had caught a sturgeon. Yu took these as signs of Heaven's mandate and sent Lin with rich gifts to bribe the Jin Left Military Supervisor Talaha for an imperial title.

sentences.zh: 撻辣許之，遣使即豫所部咨軍民所宜立，衆未及對，豫鄉人張浹越次請立豫，議遂決，乃命慶裔、昉备玺綬寳冊以立之。

translations.literal: Talaha agreed and sent envoys to Yu's territory to consult soldiers and civilians on whom they should enthrone. Before the crowd could answer, Yu's fellow townsman Zhang Xia stepped forward out of turn to ask that Yu be enthroned. The decision was settled, and Qingyi and Fang were ordered to prepare the seal cord and investiture documents to establish him.
translations.idiomatic: Talaha agreed and sent envoys to consult the army and people in Yu's territory on whom to enthrone. Before anyone could answer, Yu's fellow townsman Zhang Xia stepped forward to nominate Yu. The matter was settled, and Qingyi and Fang were ordered to prepare the regalia and investiture documents.

sentences.zh: 九月戊申，豫即偽位，赦境內，奉金正朔，稱天會八年。

translations.literal: On wushen, the ninth month, Yu took the usurped throne, pardoned those within his borders, adopted the Jin calendar, and styled his reign the eighth year of Tianhui.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen in the ninth month Yu took the throne, proclaimed an amnesty within his realm, adopted the Jin calendar, and dated his reign to Tianhui 8.

sentences.zh: 以張孝純爲丞相，李孝揚爲左丞，張柬爲右丞，李儔爲監察御史，鄭億年爲工部侍郎，王瓊爲汴京留守，子麟爲太中大夫、提領諸路兵馬兼知濟南府。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaochun was made chief councilor, Li Xiaoyang left vice councilor, Zhang Dong right vice councilor, Li Chou supervising censor, Zheng Yinian Vice Minister of Works, Wang Qiong acting prefect of Bianjing, and his son Lin Grandee of Palace Attendance, overall commander of troops on all circuits concurrent with prefect of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Zhang Xiaochun chief councilor, Li Xiaoyang left vice councilor, Zhang Dong right vice councilor, Li Chou supervising censor, Zheng Yinian Vice Minister of Works, and Wang Qiong acting prefect of Bianjing. His son Lin was made Grandee of Palace Attendance, overall commander of all circuit armies, and concurrent prefect of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 孝純始堅守太原，頗懷忠義，高宗以王衣雅厚孝純，俾衣招之，會粘罕遣人自雲中送歸豫，遂失節於賊。

translations.literal: At first Xiaochun held firm at Taiyuan and greatly cherished loyalty and righteousness. Emperor Gaozong, because Wang Yi had long been on close terms with Xiaochun, had Yi summon him; but it happened that Nianhan sent men from Yunzhong to escort him back to Yu, and so he lost his integrity to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaochun had at first defended Taiyuan steadfastly and held fast to loyalty. Emperor Gaozong, knowing that Wang Yi had long been on good terms with him, sent Yi to win him over; but Nianhan's men arrived from Yunzhong to deliver him to Liu Yu, and Xiaochun thus surrendered his honor to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 豫還東平，升爲東京。

translations.literal: Yu returned to Dongping and was promoted to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yu moved back to Dongping and was elevated to govern the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 改東京爲汴京，降南京爲歸德府。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital was renamed Bianjing, and the Southern Capital was demoted to Guide Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed the Eastern Capital Bianjing and reduced the Southern Capital to Guide Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以弟益爲北京留守，尋改汴京留守。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yi was made garrison commander of the Northern Capital; soon after he was reassigned as garrison commander of Bianjing.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his younger brother Yi to hold the Northern Capital, then shortly transferred him to serve as Bianjing garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 復降淮寧、潁昌、順昌、興仁府悉爲州。

translations.literal: Huaining, Yingchang, Shunchang, and Xingren prefectures were further demoted, all becoming zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He further demoted the prefectures of Huaining, Yingchang, Shunchang, and Xingren, reducing them all to the rank of zhou.

sentences.zh: 自以生景州，守濟南，節制東平，僭位大名，乃起四郡丁壯數千人，號「雲從子弟」。

translations.literal: Reflecting that he had been born in Jing Prefecture, had held Jinan, had commanded Dongping, and had usurped the throne at Daming, he now raised several thousand able-bodied men from four commanderies, calling them the "Cloud Retainers Youth Corps."
translations.idiomatic: Because he had been born in Jingzhou, had governed Jinan, had commanded Dongping, and had seized power at Daming, he now conscripted several thousand young men from four commanderies and styled them the "Cloud Retainers Youth Corps."

sentences.zh: 下偽詔求直言。

translations.literal: He issued a spurious edict calling for candid remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He promulgated a false edict inviting frank criticism.

sentences.zh: 十月，冊其母翟氏爲皇太后，妾錢氏爲皇后。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he ennobled his mother Lady Di as Empress Dowager and his concubine of the Qian clan as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he invested his mother, Lady Di, as Empress Dowager and his concubine Lady Qian as Empress.

sentences.zh: 錢氏，宣和內人也，習宮掖事，豫欲有所取則，故立之。

translations.literal: Lady Qian was a former palace woman from the Xuanhe era, versed in inner-palace affairs; Yu wished to take her counsel on various matters, and therefore installed her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Qian had served in the inner palace during the Xuanhe reign and knew its ways well; Yu wanted her advice on policy, and for that reason made her empress.

sentences.zh: 十一月，改明年元阜昌。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he changed the regnal year of the following year to Fuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he declared that the coming year would begin a new era named Fuchang.

sentences.zh: 方豫未僭號時，數遣人說東京副留守上官悟，及賂悟左右喬思恭與共說悟令降金，悟並斬之。

translations.literal: Before Yu had yet usurped a title, he repeatedly sent men to persuade Shangguan Wu, deputy garrison commander of the Eastern Capital, and bribed Wu's associate Qiao Sigong to join in urging Wu to surrender to the Jin; Wu had them all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Even before Yu declared himself emperor, he sent envoys again and again to win over Shangguan Wu, deputy commander at the Eastern Capital, and bribed Wu's aide Qiao Sigong to help persuade him to submit to the Jin. Wu had every one of them executed.

sentences.zh: 又招知楚州趙立，立不發書，斬其使。

translations.literal: He also tried to recruit Zhao Li, prefect of Chuzhou; Li would not even open the letter and beheaded the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He also tried to win over Zhao Li, prefect of Chuzhou, but Li refused even to break the seal on the letter and had the messenger beheaded.

sentences.zh: 復遣立友人劉偲以榜旗誘之，且曰：「吾君之故人也。」

translations.literal: He again sent Li's friend Liu Si with placards and banners to entice him, saying: "You are an old acquaintance of our lord."
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Li's friend Liu Si with proclamations and banners to lure him, saying, "You are an old friend of our ruler."

sentences.zh: 立曰：「我知有君父，不知有故人。」

translations.literal: Li said: "I know only my sovereign and father; I do not know any 'old acquaintance.'"
translations.idiomatic: Li replied, "I acknowledge only my sovereign and my father—I know no such 'old friend.'"

sentences.zh: 燒殺偲。

translations.literal: He burned [the placards] and killed Liu Si.
translations.idiomatic: He burned the proclamations and put Liu Si to death.

sentences.zh: 博州判官劉長孺以書勸豫反正，豫囚之十旬，不屈；

translations.literal: Liu Changru, judicial officer of Bozhou, wrote urging Yu to restore the rightful order; Yu imprisoned him for a hundred days, but he would not yield;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changru, a judicial officer in Bozhou, wrote urging Yu to return to allegiance to the Song; Yu held him prisoner for a hundred days, yet he would not submit;

sentences.zh: 欲官之，不受。

translations.literal: [Yu] wished to give him an office, but he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu offered him an official post, he refused it.

sentences.zh: 豫大索宋宗室，承務郎閻琦匿之，豫杖死琦。

translations.literal: Yu launched a wide search for Song imperial clansmen; Langzhong Yan Qi concealed some of them, and Yu had Qi beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yu ordered a thorough hunt for members of the Song imperial house. Yan Qi, a court gentleman, hid some of them away, and Yu had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 召迪功郎王寵，不至。

translations.literal: He summoned Langzhong Wang Chong, who did not come.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the court gentleman Wang Chong, but Chong never appeared.

sentences.zh: 文林郎李喆、尉氏令姚邦基皆棄官去。

translations.literal: Langzhong Li Zhe and Weishi magistrate Yao Bangji both abandoned their posts and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhe, a court gentleman, and Yao Bangji, magistrate of Weishi, both resigned their offices and left.

sentences.zh: 朝奉郎趙俊書甲子不書僭年，豫亦無如之何。

translations.literal: Chaofeng Lang Zhao Jun in his documents wrote only the sexagenary stem-branch year and not Yu's usurped reign year; Yu could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jun, a court gentleman, dated his documents by the sexagenary cycle alone and refused to use Yu's usurped reign year; Yu was powerless to stop him.

sentences.zh: 洪皓久陷於金，粘罕勸皓仕豫，不從，竄皓冷山。

translations.literal: Hong Hao had long been detained by the Jin; Nianhan urged Hao to serve Yu, but he refused, and [they] exiled Hao to Lengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Hao had long been held captive by the Jin. Nianhan pressed him to serve Liu Yu, but he refused and was banished to Lengshan.

sentences.zh: 處士尹惇聞豫召，逃山谷間，走蜀中。

translations.literal: The recluse Yin Dun, hearing that Yu had summoned him, fled into the mountains and valleys and made his way to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When the recluse Yin Dun learned that Yu had summoned him, he fled into the hills and made his way to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 國信副使宋汝爲以呂頤浩書勉豫忠義，豫曰：「獨不見張邦昌乎？

translations.literal: Deputy envoy of the imperial letter Song Ruwei, with a letter from Lü Yihao, urged Yu toward loyalty and righteousness; Yu said: "Have you alone not seen Zhang Bangchang?
translations.idiomatic: Song Ruwei, deputy imperial envoy, brought a letter from Lü Yihao urging Yu to return to loyalty and righteousness. Yu replied, "Have you never heard of Zhang Bangchang?

sentences.zh: 業已然，尚何言哉！」

translations.literal: The deed is already done—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: The thing is already done—what more can be said!"

sentences.zh: 滄州進士邢希載上豫書乞通宋朝，豫殺希載。

translations.literal: Xing Xizai, a jinshi of Cangzhou, submitted a letter to Yu requesting contact with the Song dynasty; Yu had Xizai killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Xizai, a jinshi degree-holder from Cangzhou, wrote to Yu asking that he reopen ties with the Song court. Yu had him executed.

sentences.zh: 是月，豫立陳東、歐陽澈廟於歸德，如唐張巡、許遠雙廟制。

translations.literal: That month, Yu established temples to Chen Dong and Ouyang Che at Guide, on the model of the paired temples of Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan in Tang times.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Yu built temples to Chen Dong and Ouyang Che at Guide, following the Tang precedent of the paired shrines to Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，知商州董先以商、虢二州叛附於豫。

translations.literal: In the second year, second month, Dong Xian, prefect of Shangzhou, rebelled with Shang and Guo prefectures and went over to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year, Dong Xian, prefect of Shangzhou, rebelled with Shang and Guo prefectures and defected to Yu.

sentences.zh: 襄陽鎮撫使桑仲上疏請正豫罪。

translations.literal: Sang Zhong, commissioner for pacification of Xiangyang, submitted a memorial asking that Yu's crimes be formally condemned.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Zhong, the Xiangyang pacification commissioner, submitted a memorial calling for Yu's crimes to be formally denounced.

sentences.zh: 朝廷尋命仲兼節制應援京城軍馬，量度事勢，復豫所陷郡。

translations.literal: The court soon ordered Zhong additionally to command the relief forces for the capital area, assess the situation, and recover the commanderies Yu had seized.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon put Zhong in charge of relief forces for the capital region as well, instructing him to weigh the situation and recover the commanderies Yu had taken.

sentences.zh: 仍命河南翟興、荊南解潛、金房王彥、德安陳規、蘄黃孔彥舟、廬壽王亨相爲應援，毋失事機。

translations.literal: It further ordered Zhai Xing of Henan, Xie Qian of Jingnan, Wang Yan of Jin-Fang, Chen Gui of De'an, Kong Yanzho of Qi-Huang, and Wang Heng of Lu-Shou each to support the effort and not miss the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: It also ordered Zhai Xing in Henan, Xie Qian in Jingnan, Wang Yan in Jin and Fang, Chen Gui in De'an, Kong Yanzho in Qi and Huang, and Wang Heng in Lu and Shou to lend support and seize the moment.

sentences.zh: 三月，仲爲其將霍明所殺，高宗聞之，授仲二子將仕郎。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zhong was killed by his own general Huo Ming; when Gaozong heard of it, he granted Zhong's two sons the rank of jiangshilang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Zhong was murdered by his subordinate Huo Ming. When Gaozong learned of it, he awarded Zhong's two sons the rank of jiangshilang.

sentences.zh: 河南鎮撫使翟興屯伊陽山，豫患之，使人招興，許以王爵。

translations.literal: Zhai Xing, Henan pacification commissioner, was encamped on Yiyang Mountain; Yu was troubled by this and sent men to recruit Xing, promising him a princely title.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Xing, the Henan pacification commissioner, was encamped on Mount Yiyang. Troubled by this, Yu sent envoys to win him over with a promise of princely rank.

sentences.zh: 興焚偽詔並戮其使。

translations.literal: Xing burned the spurious edict and executed the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Xing burned the forged edict and killed the messengers.

sentences.zh: 豫乃陰結興麾下楊偉圖之。

translations.literal: Yu then secretly won over Yang Wei among Xing's troops and plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then secretly recruited Yang Wei, one of Xing's officers, and plotted Xing's downfall.

sentences.zh: 偉殺興，持興首降豫。

translations.literal: Wei killed Xing, took his head, and surrendered to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei murdered Xing, carried off his head, and submitted to Yu.

sentences.zh: 四月丙寅，豫遷都汴。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin of the fourth month, Yu moved the capital to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day in the fourth month, Yu transferred his capital to Bian.

sentences.zh: 因奉祖考于宋太廟，尊其祖曰徽祖毅文皇帝，父爲衍祖睿仁皇帝。

translations.literal: He thereupon installed his ancestors in the Song Grand Temple, honoring his grandfather as Emperor Yizu Yiwen and his father as Emperor Yanzu Ruiren.
translations.idiomatic: He then placed his forebears in the Song Grand Temple, posthumously ennobling his grandfather as Emperor Yizu Yiwen and his father as Emperor Yanzu Ruiren.

sentences.zh: 親巡郊社。

translations.literal: He personally performed the suburban and altar rites.
translations.idiomatic: He personally conducted the suburban sacrifices at the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 是日，暴風卷旗，屋瓦皆震，士民大恐。

translations.literal: That day, a violent wind tore at the banners and shook roof tiles; officials and commoners were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: That same day a fierce wind whipped the banners and rattled roof tiles, filling officials and townspeople with dread.

sentences.zh: 豫曲赦汴人，與民約曰：「自今不肆赦，不用宦官，不度僧道。

translations.literal: Yu granted a partial amnesty to the people of Bian and made a pact with the populace, saying: "From now on there will be no indiscriminate general pardons, no employment of eunuchs, and no ordination of monks or Daoists.
translations.idiomatic: Yu issued a limited amnesty for the people of Bian and pledged to them, "Henceforth there shall be no blanket pardons, no use of eunuchs, and no ordination of monks or Daoist priests.

sentences.zh: 文武雜用，不限資格。」

translations.literal: Civil and military men shall be used interchangeably, without restriction by qualification rank."
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military talent shall be employed together, without regard to rank or qualification."

sentences.zh: 時河、淮、陝西、山東皆駐北軍，麟籍鄉兵十余萬爲皇子府十三軍。

translations.literal: At the time, Northern armies were stationed throughout the Hehuai region, Shaanxi, and Shandong; Lin registered local militia of more than a hundred thousand into thirteen armies of the Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Northern troops were then garrisoned across the Hehuai region, Shaanxi, and Shandong; Yu's son Lin enrolled more than a hundred thousand local militiamen into thirteen princely household armies.

sentences.zh: 分置河南、汴京淘沙官，兩京塚墓發掘殆盡。

translations.literal: Offices for sifting sand were established separately in Henan and Bianjing; tombs of both capitals were excavated nearly to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Sand-sifting offices were set up in Henan and Bianjing, and the tombs of both former capitals were looted almost completely.

sentences.zh: 賦斂煩苛，民不聊生。

translations.literal: Levies were burdensome and exacting; the people could scarcely survive.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes and levies were oppressive, and the common people could barely live.

sentences.zh: 五月，豫聞桑仲死，遣人招隨州李道、鄧州李橫，皆不受，執其使以聞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, upon hearing of Sang Zhong's death, Yu sent men to recruit Li Dao of Suizhou and Li Heng of Dengzhou; both refused and detained the envoys to report to the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, after learning of Sang Zhong's death, Yu sent envoys to win over Li Dao at Suizhou and Li Heng at Dengzhou. Both men refused and seized the messengers to report to the Song court.

sentences.zh: 六月，蘄、黃鎮撫使孔彥舟叛降豫，其將陳彥明率衆千餘來歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Kong Yanzho, pacification commissioner of Qi and Huang, rebelled and surrendered to Yu; his general Chen Yanming led more than a thousand men back [to Song service].
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Kong Yanzho, pacification commissioner of Qi and Huang, rebelled and went over to Yu; his officer Chen Yanming brought more than a thousand men back to the Song side.

sentences.zh: 直徽猷閣淩唐佐、尚書郎李亙、國信副使宋汝爲留偽庭，久謀疏豫虛實蠟書以聞，事泄，豫殺唐佐，亙亦遇害。

translations.literal: Ling Tangzuo of the Zhiyuan Pavilion, Langzhong of the Ministry Li Gen, and deputy imperial letter envoy Song Ruwei remained in the puppet court and for long plotted to send intelligence on Yu's strengths and weaknesses in sealed letters; when the affair leaked, Yu killed Tangzuo, and Gen also perished.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Tangzuo of the Zhiyuan Pavilion, Li Gen of the Ministry of Works, and the deputy imperial envoy Song Ruwei had remained in the puppet court and for a long time plotted to smuggle out sealed reports on Yu's strengths and weaknesses. When the plot was exposed, Yu killed Tangzuo, and Gen was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 豫以知東平府李鄴爲尚書右丞，河南鎮撫司都統制董先爲大總管府先鋒將。

translations.literal: Yu appointed Li Ye, prefect of Dongping, as Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, and Dong Xian, overall commander of the Henan Pacification Office, as vanguard general of the Grand Marshal's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yu made Li Ye, prefect of Dongping, Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, and Dong Xian, overall commander of the Henan Pacification Office, vanguard general of the Grand Marshal's Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 十二月，襄陽鎮撫使李橫敗豫兵于揚石，乘勝趣汝州，偽守彭玘以城降。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Li Heng, Xiangyang pacification commissioner, defeated Yu's troops at Yangshi, pressed the advantage toward Ruzhou, and the puppet defender Peng Chi surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Li Heng, the Xiangyang pacification commissioner, routed Yu's forces at Yangshi, pressed on toward Ruzhou, and the puppet garrison commander Peng Chi surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 豫遣劉夔與金帥撒離曷侵蜀。

translations.literal: Yu dispatched Liu Kui with the Jin commander Salihua to invade Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent Liu Kui together with the Jin commander Salihua to invade Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 執進士薛筇送豫，筇勉豫：「早圖反正，庶或全宗，孰與他日並妻子磔東市？」

translations.literal: The captured jinshi Xue Qiong was sent to Yu; Qiong urged Yu: "Plan early to restore the rightful allegiance—perhaps you may yet preserve your clan; how is that worse than someday being dismembered together with wife and children in the eastern marketplace?"
translations.idiomatic: The captured jinshi Xue Qiong was brought before Yu and urged him, "Turn back while you still can—perhaps your clan may yet be spared. Would that not be better than someday being torn apart with your wife and children in the eastern marketplace?"

sentences.zh: 豫怒，欲兵之，賴張孝純獲免。

translations.literal: Yu was enraged and wished to have him executed by military law; thanks to Zhang Xiaochun, [Qiong] was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yu flew into a rage and wanted him put to death by military law, but Zhang Xiaochun intervened and Qiong was spared.

sentences.zh: 三年正月庚申，李橫破潁順軍，偽守蘭和降。

translations.literal: In the third year, on gengshen of the first month, Li Heng broke the Yingshun army; the puppet defender Lan He surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on gengshen day in the first month, Li Heng shattered the Yingshun army and the puppet defender Lan He surrendered.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，敗豫兵于長葛。

translations.literal: On renxu, [he] defeated Yu's army at Changge.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day he defeated Yu's army at Changge.

sentences.zh: 甲子，橫引兵至潁昌府，偽安撫趙弼固守，急攻下之，弼遁，復潁昌。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Heng led troops to Yingchang Prefecture; the puppet pacification commissioner Zhao Bi held firm, but a fierce assault brought the city down; Bi fled, and Yingchang was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day Heng marched to Yingchang Prefecture. The puppet pacification commissioner Zhao Bi held out stubbornly, but a fierce assault took the city; Bi fled, and Yingchang was recovered.

sentences.zh: 二月，河南鎮撫司統制官李吉敗豫將梁進于伊陽臺，殪之。

translations.literal: In the second month, Li Ji, commanding officer of the Henan Pacification Office, defeated Yu's general Liang Jin at Yiyang Terrace and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Li Ji, a commanding officer of the Henan Pacification Office, defeated Yu's general Liang Jin at Yiyang Terrace and killed him in the battle.

sentences.zh: 三月，豫聞橫入潁昌，求援于金人。

translations.literal: In the third month, when Yu heard that Heng had entered Yingchang, he sought aid from the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, when Yu learned that Li Heng had taken Yingchang, he begged the Jurchens for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 粘罕遣兀朮赴之，豫亦遣將李成率師二萬逆戰於京城西北之牟駝岡。

translations.literal: Nianhan sent Wuzhu to the rescue; Yu also sent the general Li Cheng with an army of twenty thousand to meet the enemy at Camel Hill northwest of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan dispatched Wuzhu to relieve him, and Yu sent his general Li Cheng with twenty thousand men to give battle at Camel Hill northwest of the capital.

sentences.zh: 橫敗績，復陷潁昌。

translations.literal: Heng suffered defeat and Yingchang fell again.
translations.idiomatic: Li Heng was defeated, and Yingchang was lost once more.

sentences.zh: 橫軍本群盜，恃勇無律，勝則爭取子女金帛，故及於敗。

translations.literal: Heng's army was originally a band of brigands; relying on courage without discipline, they quarreled over women, children, gold, and silk whenever they won—and so they came to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Heng's troops had begun as a band of brigands. Bold but undisciplined, they squabbled over women, children, gold, and silk whenever they won a victory—and that was how they came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 四月，陷虢州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, [they] took Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Guo Prefecture fell.

sentences.zh: 鎮撫司統制官謝皋指腹示賊曰：「此吾赤心也！」

translations.literal: Xie Gao, commanding officer of the Pacification Office, pointed to his abdomen and showed the enemy, saying: "This is my loyal heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Xie Gao, a commanding officer of the Pacification Office, pointed to his belly and cried to the enemy, "This is my loyal heart!"

sentences.zh: 自剖心以死。

translations.literal: He cut open his own heart and died.
translations.idiomatic: He ripped open his own chest and died.

sentences.zh: 皋，開封人。

translations.literal: Gao was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Gao was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 是月，明州守將徐文以所部海舟六十艘、官軍四千餘人浮海抵鹽城，輸款於豫。

translations.literal: That month, Xu Wen, garrison commander of Mingzhou, with sixty seagoing vessels and more than four thousand government troops under his command, crossed the sea to Yancheng and offered submission to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: That month Xu Wen, the Mingzhou garrison commander, sailed across the sea with sixty warships and more than four thousand government troops to Yancheng and submitted to Yu.

sentences.zh: 文言沿海無備，二浙可襲取。

translations.literal: Wen said that the coastal defenses were unprepared and that the two Zhe provinces could be seized in a raid.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen reported that the coast was undefended and that the two Zhe provinces could be taken in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 豫大喜，以文知萊州，益海艦二十，俾寇通、泰間。

translations.literal: Yu was greatly pleased; he made Wen prefect of Laizhou, added twenty more warships, and had him raid the area between Tong and Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was delighted. He made Xu Wen prefect of Laizhou, gave him twenty more warships, and sent him to raid the region between Tongzhou and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，朝廷遣韓肖胄、胡松年使偽齊。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the court dispatched Han Xiaozhou and Hu Songnian as envoys to the puppet Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Song court sent Han Xiaozhou and Hu Songnian as envoys to the puppet Qi regime.

sentences.zh: 豫欲以臣禮見，肖胄無以應，松年曰：「均爲宋臣。」

translations.literal: Yu wished to receive them with the ceremony due a subject; Xiaozhou had no reply, but Songnian said: "We are equally subjects of Song."
translations.idiomatic: Yu wanted to receive them as if they were his subjects. Xiaozhou did not know how to answer, but Songnian said, "We are all subjects of the Song."

sentences.zh: 遂長揖不拜，豫不能屈。

translations.literal: Thereupon they made a long bow without performing the full prostration, and Yu could not bend them.
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon bowed from the waist without performing the full kowtow, and Yu could not force them to submit.

sentences.zh: 因問主上如何，松年曰：「聖主萬壽。」

translations.literal: Yu then asked how the emperor was; Songnian said: "The sage emperor enjoys ten thousand years of life."
translations.idiomatic: Yu then asked after the emperor. Songnian replied, "The sage emperor enjoys boundless longevity."

sentences.zh: 復問帝意所向，松年曰：「必欲復故疆耳。」

translations.literal: He asked again where the emperor's intent lay; Songnian said: "He surely intends to recover the former territory, nothing more."
translations.idiomatic: He asked again what the emperor intended. Songnian answered, "He means to recover the lost territories—nothing else."

sentences.zh: 豫有慚色。

translations.literal: Yu showed a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yu flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 時豫悉有梁、衛之地，翟琮屯伊陽之鳳牛山，不能孤立，突圍奔襄陽。

translations.literal: At that time Yu held all the Liang and Wei territories; Zhai Cong was encamped at Fengniu Mountain in Yiyang, unable to stand alone, and broke out to flee to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yu controlled all the Liang and Wei territories. Zhai Cong, encamped at Fengniu Mountain in Yiyang, could not hold out alone and fought his way out to flee to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，楊政遣川陝將官吳勝破豫兵於蓮花城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Yang Zheng sent the Sichuan-Shaanxi officer Wu Sheng to defeat Yu's troops at Lotus City.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Yang Zheng sent the Sichuan-Shaanxi officer Wu Sheng to defeat Yu's army at Lotus City.

sentences.zh: 十月己亥，賊將李成陷鄧州，以齊安守之；

translations.literal: On jihai of the tenth month, the rebel general Li Cheng took Deng Prefecture and left Qi'an to defend it;
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day in the tenth month the rebel general Li Cheng captured Deng Prefecture and left Qi'an to hold it;

sentences.zh: 癸卯，陷襄陽，李橫奔荊南，知隨州李道棄城走。

translations.literal: On guimao, [he] took Xiangyang; Li Heng fled to Jingnan, and Li Dao, prefect of Suizhou, abandoned his city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day he took Xiangyang. Li Heng fled to Jingnan, and Li Dao, prefect of Suizhou, abandoned the city and ran.

sentences.zh: 成據襄陽，以王嵩知隨州。

translations.literal: Cheng held Xiangyang and appointed Wang Song prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng held Xiangyang and installed Wang Song as prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，陷郢州，守臣李簡遁，豫以荊超知州事。

translations.literal: On jiachen, [they] took Ying Prefecture; the defending official Li Jian fled, and Yu put Jing Chao in charge of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Ying Prefecture fell. The defending official Li Jian fled, and Yu put Jing Chao in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賊將王彥先自亳引兵至壽春，將窺江南。

translations.literal: The rebel general Wang Yanxian led troops from Bo to Shouchun, intending to spy out an opportunity against lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Wang Yanxian marched from Bo to Shouchun, intending to probe for a chance to strike south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 劉光世駐軍建康，扼馬家渡，遣酈瓊領所部駐無爲軍，爲濠、壽聲援，賊乃還。

translations.literal: Liu Guangshi encamped at Jiankang, blocking Majia Crossing; he sent Li Qiong with his forces to garrison Wuwei Army as a screen for Hao and Shou, and the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi was encamped at Jiankang, holding Majia Crossing. He sent Li Qiong with his troops to garrison Wuwei Army as support for Hao and Shou, and the rebels then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十二月，金人遣李永壽、王翊來報聘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Jurchens sent Li Yongshou and Wang Yi on a return courtesy mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Jurchens sent Li Yongshou and Wang Yi on a return diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 永壽等驕倨，請還豫俘及西北士民之流寓者，復要畫江以益豫。

translations.literal: Yongshou and the others were arrogant and imperious; they requested the return of prisoners held by Yu and displaced people from the northwest, and further demanded drawing the [Yangtze] river boundary to enlarge Yu's domain.
translations.idiomatic: Yongshou and his party were haughty and overbearing. They demanded the return of captives held by Yu and displaced people from the northwest, and also insisted on fixing the Yangtze as the border to expand Yu's territory.

sentences.zh: 監廣州鹽稅吳伸上書請討豫，謂「金人雖強，實不足慮，賊豫雖微，實爲可憂。

translations.literal: Wu Shen, supervisor of Guangzhou salt taxes, submitted a memorial requesting a campaign against Yu, stating: "Although the Jurchens are strong, they are in truth not worth worrying over; although the rebel Yu is small, he is truly cause for concern.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shen, who supervised the salt tax at Guangzhou, submitted a memorial urging an expedition against Yu. He argued, "The Jurchens may be strong, but they are not the real worry; the rebel Yu may be small, but he is the one we should fear.

sentences.zh: 今敵使在廷，宜陽許而陰圖之，乘其不疑，可一戰擒也。」

translations.literal: Now that the enemy envoys are at court, we should agree openly while plotting in secret; catching them off guard, we could capture them in a single battle."
translations.idiomatic: With the enemy envoys now at court, we should agree to their terms in public while plotting against them in secret. Taken by surprise, they could be seized in a single stroke."

sentences.zh: 四年正月，翰林學士綦崇禮言：「豫父子倚重金人，且永壽等從豫所來，畫江之請必出於豫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, first month, Hanlin Academician Qi Chongli said: "The Yu father and son rely heavily on the Jurchens; moreover, Yongshou and the others came from Yu's domain—the request to fix the boundary at the river must have originated with Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, Hanlin Academician Qi Chongli said, "The Yu father and son lean heavily on the Jurchens, and Yongshou's party came from Yu's territory—the demand to fix the border at the river must have come from Yu himself.

sentences.zh: 觀其奸謀，在窺吾境土。

translations.literal: Judging from this crafty scheme, their aim is to encroach upon our territory.
translations.idiomatic: From this treacherous design it is clear that their aim is to encroach on our lands.

sentences.zh: 恐既通使，人情必解弛，宜戒將帥愈益置守。

translations.literal: I fear that once envoys are exchanged, public morale will surely relax; the generals should be warned all the more to strengthen defenses.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that once diplomatic exchanges begin, public resolve will slacken. Our commanders should be warned all the more to tighten their defenses.

sentences.zh: 縱和議成，亦未可馳備。」

translations.literal: Even if peace talks succeed, we must not slacken preparedness."
translations.idiomatic: Even if a peace agreement is reached, we must not let our guard down."

sentences.zh: 既而朝廷遣章誼使金，至雲中。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the court sent Zhang Yi as envoy to Jin; he reached Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the court dispatched Zhang Yi as envoy to the Jin and he reached Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 粘罕答書約毋駐軍淮南，誼不屈，還過汴，豫欲留之，以計獲免。

translations.literal: Nianhan replied with a letter stipulating that no troops be stationed in Huainan; Yi would not yield; on his return he passed through Bian, and Yu wished to detain him, but Yi escaped by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan replied with a letter demanding that no Song troops remain in Huainan. Zhang Yi refused to yield. On his return he passed through Bian, and Yu tried to detain him, but Yi escaped by a ruse.

sentences.zh: 熙河路馬步軍總管關師古與豫兵戰于左要嶺，敗績，遂降賊。

translations.literal: Guan Shigu, overall commander of cavalry and infantry on the Xihe Circuit, fought Yu's troops at Zuoyao Ridge, suffered defeat, and then surrendered to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Shigu, overall commander of cavalry and infantry on the Xihe Circuit, fought Yu's army at Zuoyao Ridge, was defeated, and then surrendered to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 洮、岷之地盡歸豫矣。

translations.literal: The lands of Tao and Min all passed to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The territories of Tao and Min all fell into Yu's hands.

sentences.zh: 二月，豫策進士。

translations.literal: In the second month, Yu held the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Yu conducted the jinshi civil examination.

sentences.zh: 五月，知壽春府羅興叛降豫。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Luo Xing, prefect of Shouchun, rebelled and surrendered to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Luo Xing, prefect of Shouchun, rebelled and went over to Yu.

sentences.zh: 舒、蘄等州制置使岳飛復襄陽，李成遁，尋復唐州。

translations.literal: Yue Fei, commissioner for the disposition of forces in Shu, Qi, and other prefectures, recovered Xiangyang; Li Cheng fled, and soon Tang Prefecture was recovered as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei, commissioner for Shu, Qi, and neighboring prefectures, recovered Xiangyang. Li Cheng fled, and Tang Prefecture was soon retaken as well.

sentences.zh: 六月，復隨州，磔偽守王嵩於襄陽市。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Suizhou was recovered, and the puppet prefect Wang Song was dismembered in the marketplace at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Suizhou was recovered, and the puppet prefect Wang Song was torn apart in the marketplace at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 七月，復鄧州，語在《飛傳》。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Deng Prefecture was recovered; the account is given in the Biography of Yue Fei.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Deng Prefecture was recovered; the details are recorded in the Biography of Yue Fei.

sentences.zh: 豫聞岳飛取襄、鄧，遂乞師于金人。

translations.literal: When Yu heard that Yue Fei had taken Xiangyang and Dengzhou, he begged the Jurchens for troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu learned that Yue Fei had retaken Xiangyang and Dengzhou, he pleaded with the Jurchens for military aid.

sentences.zh: 偽奉議郎羅誘上南征策，豫大喜。

translations.literal: The false Gentleman Consultant Luo You submitted a strategy for a southern campaign; Yu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Luo You, a courtier in Liu Yu's puppet regime, proposed a southern expedition—and Yu was delighted.

sentences.zh: 奪民舟五百載戰具，以徐文爲前軍，聲言攻定海。

translations.literal: He seized five hundred civilian boats to carry war equipment, made Xu Wen the vanguard, and proclaimed an attack on Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred civilian vessels were requisitioned for munitions; Xu Wen led the advance force while proclamations announced an assault on Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 九月，豫下偽詔，有「混一六合」之言，遣子麟入寇，及誘金人宗輔、撻辣、兀朮分道南侵，步兵自楚、承進，騎兵由泗趨滁。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Yu issued a false edict containing words of 'unifying the six directions,' sent his son Lin to invade, and moreover induced the Jin men Zongfu, Talaha, and Wuzhu to invade south by separate routes—infantry advancing from Chu and Chengzhou, cavalry rushing toward Chuzhou via Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That September Liu Yu promulgated a counterfeit decree proclaiming the 'unification of all under Heaven,' dispatched his son Lin on a raid, and persuaded the Jin generals Zongfu, Talaha, and Wuzhu to strike south on divergent routes—foot soldiers from Chu and Chengzhou, horsemen from Sizhou toward Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 復遣偽知樞密院盧緯請師于金主，金主集諸將議，粘罕、希尹難之，獨宗輔以爲可。

translations.literal: Again he sent the false Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Lu Wei to request troops from the Jin sovereign; the Jin sovereign convened the generals to discuss—Nianhan and Xiyin objected, only Zongfu considered it feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Yu also dispatched Lu Wei, his commissioner of military affairs, to beg the Jin emperor for reinforcements. The emperor summoned his commanders: Nianhan and Xiyin opposed the plan, but Zongfu alone argued it could work.

sentences.zh: 乃以宗輔權左副元帥，撻辣權右副元帥，調渤海漢軍五萬應豫。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zongfu was appointed acting Left Deputy Marshal, Talaha acting Right Deputy Marshal, and fifty thousand Bohai Han troops were mobilized to support Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Zongfu received command as acting left deputy marshal and Talaha as right deputy; fifty thousand Han troops from the Bohai region were levied to answer Yu's call.

sentences.zh: 以兀朮嘗渡江，習知險易，俾將前軍。

translations.literal: Because Wuzhu had once crossed the river and was familiar with the difficult and easy terrain, he was made to lead the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu, who had crossed the Yangzi before and knew its hazards well, was placed at the head of the army.

sentences.zh: 豫以麟領東南道行台尚書令。

translations.literal: Yu made Lin hold the post of Acting Grand Chancellor of the Southeast Circuit Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu appointed his son Lin director of the southeastern regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 朝廷震恐。

translations.literal: The court trembled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: The Song court was seized with panic.

sentences.zh: 或勸帝他幸，趙鼎曰：「戰而不捷，去未晚也。」

translations.literal: Some urged the emperor to seek refuge elsewhere; Zhao Ding said: 'If we fight and do not prevail, it will not be too late to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Some counseled the emperor to relocate the capital; Zhao Ding replied, 'If we give battle and fail, flight will still be in time.

sentences.zh: 張俊曰：「避將安之？」

translations.literal: Zhang Jun said: 'If we flee, where shall we go?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun asked, 'Flee—and flee to where?

sentences.zh: 遂決意親征。

translations.literal: Thereupon he resolved to lead the expedition in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thus resolved to take the field himself.

sentences.zh: 壬申，豫兵與金人分道渡淮，楚州守臣樊序棄城走，淮東宣撫使韓世忠自承州退保鎮江。

translations.literal: On renshen, Yu's troops and the Jin men crossed the Huai by separate routes; the defender of Chuzhou Fan Xu abandoned the city and fled; the Huaidong Military Commissioner Han Shizhong withdrew from Chengzhou to defend Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day, puppet-Qi and Jin forces forded the Huai on separate fronts. Fan Xu, commandant of Chuzhou, deserted his post; Han Shizhong, commissioner for eastern Huai, fell back from Chengzhou to the walls of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 十月丙子朔，詔張俊援世忠，劉光世移軍建康。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month, bingzi, an edict ordered Zhang Jun to reinforce Shizhong and Liu Guangshi to move his army to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the tenth month—bingzi—the court ordered Zhang Jun to reinforce Han Shizhong and Liu Guangshi to shift his forces to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 世忠復還揚州。

translations.literal: Shizhong again returned to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong then marched back to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 起張浚爲侍讀。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun was recalled to serve as Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was recalled from retirement to resume his post as imperial reader.

sentences.zh: 戊子，韓世忠戰於大儀，己丑，解元戰於承州，皆捷。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Han Shizhong fought at Dayi; on jichou, Xie Yuan fought at Chengzhou—both were victorious.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Han Shizhong won at Dayi; the next day Xie Yuan routed the enemy at Chengzhou—twin victories.

sentences.zh: 丙申，豫露榜有窺江之言。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Yu posted a proclamation containing words of spying on the river.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Yu's armies put up placards hinting at designs on the Yangzi crossing.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，帝發臨安。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the emperor departed from Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the emperor left the temporary capital at Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬子，下詔討豫，始暴豫罪惡，士氣大振，欲濟江決戰。
