translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on renzi, an edict was issued to campaign against Yu, first exposing Yu's crimes—morale soared greatly and they wished to cross the river for a decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renzi, the court proclaimed a punitive expedition against Liu Yu, publicly enumerating his crimes; spirits soared and troops clamored to cross the Yangzi for a final reckoning.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎曰：「退固不可，渡江亦非策。

translations.literal: Zhao Ding said: 'Retreat is certainly not permissible, but crossing the river is also not a strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding cautioned, 'We cannot simply retreat—but crossing the river is no strategy either.

sentences.zh: 豫猶不親來，至尊豈可與逆雛決勝負哉？」

translations.literal: Yu still does not come in person—how can His Majesty contend for victory with a rebellious whelp?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu has not even come himself—should the Son of Heaven stoop to settle scores with a traitor's pup?

sentences.zh: 淮西將王師晟、張琦合兵復南壽春府，執偽知州王靖。

translations.literal: The western Huai generals Wang Shisheng and Zhang Qi combined forces and recovered southern Shouchun Prefecture, seizing the false prefect Wang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In western Huai, Wang Shisheng and Zhang Qi joined ranks, retook Shouchun, and captured the puppet prefect Wang Jing.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬辰，岳飛遣將牛皋、徐慶敗金人於廬州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, renchen, Yue Fei dispatched generals Niu Gao and Xu Qing to defeat the Jin men at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renchen, Yue Fei sent Niu Gao and Xu Qing to crush Jin forces at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚子，金人退師，遣使告麟，麟棄輜重宵遁，語在《世忠傳》。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the Jin men withdrew their army and sent envoys to inform Lin; Lin abandoned baggage and fled by night—the account is in the 'Biography of Shizhong.'
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the Jin army pulled back and notified Lin; Lin abandoned his supply train and fled under cover of night—the full account appears in Han Shizhong's biography.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，淮西將酈瓊復光州，偽守許約降。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, the western Huai general Li Qiong recovered Guang Prefecture; the false defender Xu Yue surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year five, Li Qiong of western Huai retook Guangzhou as the puppet garrison commander Xu Yue capitulated.

sentences.zh: 閏二月，豫將商元攻信陽軍，知軍事舒繼明死之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary second month, Yu's general Shang Yuan attacked Xinyang Circuit; the military superintendent Shu Jiming died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the leap second month, Shang Yuan of Yu's army besieged Xinyang; Shu Jiming, who commanded its defense, fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 七月，豫廢明堂爲講武殿，暴風連日。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Yu converted the Bright Hall into a martial-training hall; violent winds lasted for days.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Liu Yu turned the Imperial Ancestral Hall into a drill hall—and tempests raged for days on end.

sentences.zh: 八月，陷光州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, they captured Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Guangzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 十月，豫令民鬻子依商稅法許貫陌而收其算。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Yu ordered the people to sell their children according to the merchant tax law, permitting payment by full string and collecting the assessment.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yu decreed that parents selling children would be taxed as merchants—full strings accepted, every transaction assessed.

sentences.zh: 豫獻《海道圖》及戰船木樣于金主亶。

translations.literal: Yu presented the 'Sea Route Map' and wooden models of war ships to the Jin sovereign Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent the Jin emperor Dan charts of sea routes and scale models of warships.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，豫聚兵淮陽，韓世忠引兵急圍之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, Yu massed troops at Huaiyang; Han Shizhong led troops in rapid siege.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year six Yu concentrated forces at Huaiyang; Han Shizhong hurried to encircle him.

sentences.zh: 賊守將連舉六烽，兀朮與劉猊合兵來援，皆爲世忠所敗。

translations.literal: The rebel defending generals raised six signal fires in succession; Wuzhu and Liu Ni combined forces to come to the rescue—all were defeated by Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: The besieged garrison lit beacon after beacon—six in all—until Wuzhu and Liu Ni marched to relieve them; Han Shizhong defeated them both.

sentences.zh: 六月，築劉龍城以窺淮西，王師晟破之，執華知剛，俘其衆而還。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, they built Liulong Fort to spy on western Huai; Wang Shisheng broke it, seized Hua Zhigang, captured his men and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the rebels fortified Liulongcheng to threaten western Huai; Wang Shisheng stormed it, took Hua Zhigang prisoner, and marched home with captives in tow.

sentences.zh: 九月，豫罷沿海互市。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Yu abolished coastal mutual markets.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liu Yu shut down the coastal trade ports.

sentences.zh: 張孝純謂豫曰：「聞南人久治舟，一旦乘風北濟，將不利於我。」

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaochun said to Yu: 'I hear the southerners have long maintained boats; if they once ride the wind northward across the river, it will be unfavorable for us.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaochun warned Yu, 'The Song have spent years building a fleet. One fair wind carrying them north across the water—and we are undone.

sentences.zh: 豫懼，故罷之。

translations.literal: Yu was afraid, and therefore abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu took fright and closed the ports.

sentences.zh: 豫聞帝親征，告急于金主亶，領三省事宗磐曰：「先帝立豫者，欲豫辟疆保境，我得按兵息民也。

translations.literal: Yu, hearing the emperor was leading a campaign in person, urgently reported to the Jin sovereign Dan; Zong Pan, who headed the Three Departments, said: 'The former emperor established Yu intending that Yu should open frontiers and preserve borders, so that we could hold our armies and rest the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu learned the Song emperor was taking the field himself, he begged Jin emperor Dan for aid. Zong Pan, chief of the Three Departments, argued: 'Our late emperor installed Liu Yu so he would guard the frontier and keep the peace—leaving us free to sheathe our swords and give the realm rest.

sentences.zh: 今豫進不能取，退不能守，兵連禍結，休息無期。

translations.literal: Now Yu advances yet cannot take, retreats yet cannot hold—war links with calamity without end, rest without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Now he advances without conquering, retreats without holding; war drags on, disaster compounds, and there is no end to the toll.

sentences.zh: 從之則豫收其利，而我實受弊，奈何許之！」

translations.literal: If we follow this, Yu reaps the profit while we actually suffer harm—how can we assent!
translations.idiomatic: Grant this request and Yu alone gains; we alone pay the price. How can we agree?

sentences.zh: 金主報豫自行，姑遣兀朮提兵黎陽以觀釁。

translations.literal: The Jin sovereign replied to Yu to act on his own, for the moment dispatching Wuzhu to lead troops at Liyang to watch for provocation.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor told Yu to manage on his own—for now dispatching Wuzhu to Liyang with an army to watch for an opening.

sentences.zh: 豫於是以麟領東南道行台尚書令，李鄴行台右丞，馮長寧行台戶部，許清臣兵馬大總管，李成、孔彥舟、關師古爲將，籍民兵三十萬，分三道入寇。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon made Lin lead the Southeast Circuit Regional Secretariat as Grand Chancellor, Li Ye as Right Commissioner of the Regional Secretariat, Feng Changning as Regional Secretariat Household Department, Xu Qingchen as Grand Marshal of Arms and Horses, Li Cheng, Kong Yanz Zhou, and Guan Shigu as generals, registered three hundred thousand militia, and divided into three routes to invade.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu mustered three hundred thousand militia in three columns: his son Lin as commander of the southeastern secretariat; Li Ye, Feng Changning, and Xu Qingchen in key staff posts; Li Cheng, Kong Yanz Zhou, and Guan Shigu as field generals—and sent the whole host south in a triple invasion.

sentences.zh: 麟總中路兵，由壽春犯廬州；

translations.literal: Lin commanded the central-route army, proceeding from Shouchun to attack Luzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Lin led the center, marching from Shouchun against Luzhou;

sentences.zh: 猊率東路兵，取紫荊山出渦口以犯定遠；

translations.literal: Ni led the eastern-route army, taking Zijing Mountain and exiting Wo Mouth to attack Dingyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Ni commanded the eastern wing, descending from Zijing Mountain through Wo Kou toward Dingyuan;

sentences.zh: 西兵趨光州寇六安，彥舟統之。

translations.literal: The western army hastened toward Guangzhou to raid Lu'an; Yanz Zhou commanded it.
translations.idiomatic: The western column struck from Guangzhou toward Lu'an under Kong Yanz Zhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，猊兵阻韓世忠不得前，還順昌。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Ni's army was blocked by Han Shizhong and could not advance, and returned to Shunchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Liu Ni's advance stalled before Han Shizhong's line; he withdrew to Shunchang.

sentences.zh: 麟兵從淮西系三浮橋以濟，賊衆十萬次濠、壽間。

translations.literal: Lin's army from western Huai linked three pontoon bridges to cross; one hundred thousand rebels encamped between Hao and Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's force crossed the Huai on three pontoon bridges; a hundred thousand rebel troops massed between Hao and Shou.

sentences.zh: 江東安撫使張俊拒戰，詔並以淮西屬俊，命殿帥楊沂中至泗州與俊合，比至濠而劉光世已棄合肥矣。

translations.literal: The Jiangdong Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun resisted battle; an edict also placed western Huai under Jun, ordering Palace Commander Yang Yizhong to reach Sizhou and join Jun—by the time they reached Hao, Liu Guangshi had already abandoned Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, pacification commissioner for Jiangdong, took up the defense; the court placed all of western Huai under his command and sent the palace guard commander Yang Yizhong to link up with him at Sizhou—but by the time they reached Hao, Liu Guangshi had already abandoned Hefei.

sentences.zh: 張浚遣人星馳採石諭光世曰：「敢濟者斬。」

translations.literal: Zhang Jun sent a man galloping at full speed to Caishi to instruct Guangshi: 'Whoever dares cross the river shall be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun dispatched a rider at full gallop to Caishi with orders for Guangshi: 'Any man who attempts a crossing dies.

sentences.zh: 光世不得已還廬州，與沂中相應。

translations.literal: Guangshi had no choice but to return to Luzhou and coordinate with Yizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi had no choice but to march back to Luzhou and coordinate with Yang Yizhong.

sentences.zh: 統制王德、酈瓊出安豐，遇賊三將軍皆敗之。

translations.literal: Regimental commanders Wang De and Li Qiong sortied from Anfeng, encountered three rebel generals and defeated them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De and Li Qiong led troops out of Anfeng and routed three rebel generals in succession.

sentences.zh: 猊衆數萬過定遠，欲趨宣化犯建康。

translations.literal: Several tens of thousands of Ni's troops passed Dingyuan, intending to hasten toward Xuanhua to attack Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands under Liu Ni passed Dingyuan, angling through Xuanhua toward Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 沂中遇猊兵於越家坊，破之；

translations.literal: Yizhong encountered Ni's troops at Yuejia Lane and broke them;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yizhong intercepted Ni at Yuejia Lane and shattered his column;

sentences.zh: 又遇於藕塘，大破之。

translations.literal: Again encountered them at Outang and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: then caught him again at Outang and broke him completely.

sentences.zh: 猊遁，麟聞亦拔砦走，麟兵有自書鄉貫姓名而縊者，豫由此失人心。

translations.literal: Ni fled; hearing this, Lin also broke camp and fled; among Lin's soldiers some wrote their native place and name and hanged themselves—Yu thereby lost the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ni fled; when Lin heard, he too broke camp and ran. Some of Lin's soldiers wrote their names and home districts on slips and hanged themselves. From this Liu Yu lost the people's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 金人聞麟等敗，詰豫罪狀，始有廢豫意矣。

translations.literal: The Jin men, hearing of Lin's defeat, questioned Yu's offenses—thereupon arose the intention to depose Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When word of Lin's rout reached the Jin court, they pressed Liu Yu to account for his failures—and first began to consider removing him.

sentences.zh: 豫覺，請立麟爲太子，以覘其意。

translations.literal: Yu perceived this and requested to establish Lin as crown prince, to probe their intention.
translations.idiomatic: Sensing danger, Yu petitioned to name Lin his heir—testing how the Jin would respond.

sentences.zh: 金人乃答豫曰：「徐當遣人咨訪河南百姓。」

translations.literal: The Jin men then replied to Yu: 'For the time being we should send men to consult the common people of Henan.'
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court answered evasively: 'We must first send envoys to sound out the people of Henan.'

sentences.zh: 七年春，豫策進士。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, Yu conducted the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year seven Liu Yu held civil-service examinations for jinshi degrees.

sentences.zh: 遣諜縱火淮甸，燔劉光世帑藏。

translations.literal: He sent spies to set fire in the Huai region, burning Liu Guangshi's treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: Spies were sent to torch stores across the Huai plain, including Liu Guangshi's treasury.

sentences.zh: 二月，又焚鎮江。

translations.literal: In the second month, they again burned Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month they struck again, burning Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 豫自麟敗，意沮氣奪。

translations.literal: Since Lin's defeat, Yu's intent was discouraged and his spirit seized.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin's defeat Liu Yu's spirits collapsed.

sentences.zh: 中原遺民，日望王師。

translations.literal: The remnant people of the Central Plains daily looked for the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: In the lost lands of the north, people waited day after day for the Song armies to return.

sentences.zh: 三月，帝進駐建康。

translations.literal: In the third month, the emperor advanced and garrisoned Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the emperor moved his headquarters to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 八月，統制酈瓊執呂祉，以兵三萬叛降豫，尋殺祉。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, regimental commander Li Qiong seized Lü Zhi, rebelled with thirty thousand troops and surrendered to Yu, and soon killed Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Li Qiong seized his superior Lü Zhi, defected to Liu Yu with thirty thousand men, and soon murdered him.

sentences.zh: 豫聞瓊降大喜，御文德殿見之，授瓊靜難軍節度使、知拱州。

translations.literal: Yu, hearing Qiong's surrender, was greatly pleased; he received him in the Wende Hall and appointed Qiong Military Commissioner of the Jingnan Army and prefect of Gongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted by Li Qiong's defection, Liu Yu received him in the Hall of Literary Virtue and made him military commissioner of Jingnan with governorship of Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 瓊勸豫入寇，豫復乞師金人，且言瓊欲自效。

translations.literal: Qiong urged Yu to invade; Yu again begged troops from the Jin and added Qiong wished to offer his service.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiong urged another southern raid; Liu Yu again begged the Jin for troops, boasting that his new general was eager to prove his worth.

sentences.zh: 金人恐豫兵衆難制，欲以計除之，乃佯言瓊降恐詐，命散其兵。

translations.literal: The Jin men feared Yu's troops were numerous and hard to control, wished to remove him by stratagem, and therefore falsely said Qiong's surrender was feared to be a ruse and ordered his troops dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin feared Liu Yu's swollen armies were beyond control and plotted his downfall—pretending Li Qiong's surrender might be a trick, they ordered his forces disbanded.

sentences.zh: 金人業已廢豫，而豫日益請兵，遂以女真萬戶束拔爲元帥府左都監屯太原，渤海萬戶大撻不也爲右都監屯河間。

translations.literal: The Jin had already decided to depose Yu, yet Yu daily increased his requests for troops; thereupon the Jurchen commander Shubo was made Left Overseer of the Marshal's Headquarters and garrisoned at Taiyuan, and the Bohai commander Dadabuye was made Right Overseer and garrisoned at Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Jin had already decided to remove Liu Yu, he kept demanding more troops—so they posted the Jurchen commander Shubo as left overseer at Taiyuan and the Bohai commander Dadabuye as right overseer at Hejian, tightening their grip on the region.

sentences.zh: 於是尚書省奏豫治國無狀，當廢。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of State submitted that Yu's governance was misshapen and he should be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of State then memorialized that Liu Yu had governed so wretchedly he must be removed.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙午，廢豫爲蜀王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on bingwu, Yu was deposed and made Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu in the eleventh month Liu Yu was stripped of power and given the hollow title Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 初，金主先令撻辣、兀朮偽稱南侵至汴，紿麟出至武城，麾騎翼而擒之，因馳至城中。

translations.literal: Initially, the Jin sovereign first ordered Talaha and Wuzhu to feign a southern invasion as far as Bian, deceived Lin into coming out to Wucheng, waved horsemen to flank and seize him, then galloped into the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor's plan began with Talaha and Wuzhu feigning a southern advance on Bian—luring Lin out to Wucheng, where cavalry closed from the flanks and seized him, then racing into the city.

sentences.zh: 豫方射講武殿，兀朮從三騎突入東華門，下馬執其手，偕至宣德門，強乘以羸馬，露刃夾之，囚于金明池。

translations.literal: Yu was just practicing archery at the Martial Training Hall; Wuzhu burst through the Donghua Gate with three horsemen, dismounted and grasped his hand, together reached the Xuanede Gate, forced him onto an emaciated horse with bared blades flanking him, and imprisoned him at Jinming Pond.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu was at the drill hall practicing archery when Wuzhu burst through the East Flowery Gate with three riders, seized his hand, marched him to the Xuanede Gate, forced him onto a worn-out nag with naked blades at his sides, and locked him in Jinming Pond.

sentences.zh: 翼日，集百官宣詔責豫，以鐵騎數千圍宮門，遣小校巡閭巷間，揚言曰：「自今不僉汝爲軍，不取汝免行錢，爲汝敲殺貌事人，請汝舊主少帝來此。」

translations.literal: The next day, the hundred officials were assembled and an edict was proclaimed rebuking Yu; with several thousand armored horsemen surrounding the palace gates, small officers were sent to patrol the lanes and alleys, proclaiming: 'From now on we will not conscript you as soldiers, will not take your exemption fees, will beat and kill for you those who treat service with contempt—call your former lord the Young Emperor to come here.
translations.idiomatic: The next day a formal decree condemned Liu Yu before the assembled bureaucracy. Thousands of armored horsemen ringed the palace gates while patrols moved through the streets proclaiming: 'No more conscription, no more war levies—we will deal harshly with anyone who scorns his duty. Bring back your old emperor, the captive lord of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 由是人心稍安。

translations.literal: Thereupon the people's hearts were somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: The populace took some comfort from this.

sentences.zh: 置行台尚書省於汴，以張孝純權行台左丞相。

translations.literal: The Regional Secretariat was established at Bian; Zhang Xiaochun was made acting Left Chancellor of the Regional Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: A regional secretariat was installed at Bian, with Zhang Xiaochun as acting left chancellor.

sentences.zh: 偽丞相張昂知孟州，李鄴知代州，李成、孔彥舟、酈瓊、關師古各予一郡。

translations.literal: The false chancellor Zhang Ang was made prefect of Mengzhou, Li Ye of Daizhou; Li Cheng, Kong Yanz Zhou, Li Qiong, and Guan Shigu each were given a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The former puppet officials were reassigned: Zhang Ang to Mengzhou, Li Ye to Daizhou; Li Cheng, Kong Yanz Zhou, Li Qiong, and Guan Shigu each received a commandery.

sentences.zh: 以女真胡沙虎爲汴京留守，李儔副之。

translations.literal: The Jurchen Hushahu was made Bian capital intendant, with Li Chou as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen officer Hushahu became military governor of Bianjing, assisted by Li Chou.

sentences.zh: 諸軍悉令歸農，聽宮人出嫁。

translations.literal: All armies were ordered to return to farming; palace women were permitted to marry out.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers were sent back to their fields; palace women were free to marry.

sentences.zh: 得金一百二十余萬兩、銀一千六百余萬兩、米九十余萬斛、絹二百七十萬匹、錢九千八百七十余萬緡。

translations.literal: Obtained gold of more than 1.2 million taels, silver more than 16 million taels, rice more than 900,000 hu, silk more than 2.7 million bolts, cash more than 98.7 million strings.
translations.idiomatic: The confiscated hoard included over 1.2 million taels of gold, 16 million of silver, 900,000 hu of grain, 2.7 million bolts of silk, and nearly 99 million strings of copper cash.

sentences.zh: 豫求哀，撻辣曰：「昔趙氏少帝出京，百姓然頂煉臂，號泣之聲聞於遠邇。

translations.literal: Yu pleaded for mercy; Talaha said: 'In the past when the Young Emperor of Zhao left the capital, the common people burned their crowns and branded their arms—the sound of wailing was heard near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu begged for mercy. Talaha said coldly, 'When the young Zhao emperor was taken from the capital, people burned their hair and branded their arms—the sound of weeping carried for miles.

sentences.zh: 今汝廢，無一人憐汝者，何不自責也。」

translations.literal: Now that you are deposed, not one person pities you—why do you not blame yourself?
translations.idiomatic: You are deposed, and not a soul mourns for you. Have you no shame?

sentences.zh: 豫語塞，迫之行，願居相州韓琦宅，許之。

translations.literal: Yu was speechless; compelled to depart, he wished to dwell in Han Qi's mansion at Xiangzhou—this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu had no answer. Driven into exile, he asked to live in Han Qi's old house at Xiangzhou—the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 後並其子麟徙於臨潢，封豫爲曹王，賜田以居之。

translations.literal: Later both he and his son Lin were transferred to Linhuang; Yu was enfeoffed as Prince of Cao and granted fields to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Lin were exiled to Linhuang; Liu Yu received the title Prince of Cao and farmland enough to live on.

sentences.zh: 紹興十三年六月卒，是年金皇統三年也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year of Shaoxing he died—it was the third year of Jin Huangtong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of Shaoxing 13—Jin Huangtong 3 by the northern calendar.

sentences.zh: 豫僭號凡八年，廢時年六十五。

translations.literal: Yu usurped the title for eight years altogether; at deposition he was sixty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu had reigned in pretense for eight years; he was sixty-five when deposed.

sentences.zh: 先是，齊地數見怪異，有梟鳴于後苑，龍撼宣德門滅「宣德」二字，有星隕于平原鎮。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Qi territory strange phenomena were repeatedly seen: an owl cried in the rear garden; a dragon shook the Xuanede Gate and erased the two characters 'Xuanede'; a star fell at Pingyuan Town.
translations.idiomatic: Before his fall, Qi lands were troubled by omens: an owl shrieked in the imperial park; lightning struck the Xuanede Gate and obliterated its inscription; a star fell on Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 識者謂禍不出百日，豫怒殺之。

translations.literal: Those who understood said calamity would not exceed a hundred days—Yu in anger killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Soothsayers predicted disaster within a hundred days; in fury Liu Yu had them executed.

sentences.zh: 未幾果廢。

translations.literal: Before long he was indeed deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon enough he was overthrown.

sentences.zh: 初，偽麟府路經略使折可求以事抵雲中，左監軍撒離曷密諭可求代豫。

translations.literal: Initially, the false Jinfu Circuit Military Commissioner Zhe Keqiu, having business reaching Yunzhong, the Left Military Inspector Saliehe secretly instructed Keqiu to replace Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Zhe Keqiu—the puppet commissioner of Jinfu Circuit—traveled on business to Yunzhong, where the Jurchen inspector Saliehe quietly sounded him out about replacing Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 後撻辣有歸疆之議，恐可求𡙇望，鴆殺之。

translations.literal: Later Talaha had a proposal to return territory; fearing Keqiu would obstruct it, he poisoned and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Talaha later broached returning lost territory, he feared Zhe Keqiu would resist and had him poisoned.

sentences.zh: 豫之僭逆也，馬定國進《君臣名分論》，祝簡獻《遷都》、《國馬賦》，語多指斥；

translations.literal: During Yu's usurpation and rebellion, Ma Dingguo presented the 'Treatise on the Names and Standings of Ruler and Subject,' Zhu Jian submitted 'On Moving the Capital' and 'Rhapsody on the State's Horses'—the words mostly cast blame;
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Liu Yu's reign, Ma Dingguo submitted 'On the Proper Relations of Ruler and Subject,' while Zhu Jian offered essays on moving the capital and on the state's horses—both laced with veiled rebuke;

sentences.zh: 又如許清臣毀景靈宮，孟邦雄發永安陵，蹠犬吠堯，蓋無責焉。

translations.literal: Then again such as Xu Qingchen's destruction of the Jingling Palace, Meng Bangxiong's opening of the Yong'an Mausoleum—a robber's dog barking at Yao, in the end none were held accountable.
translations.idiomatic: Likewise Xu Qingchen razed the Jingling Shrine and Meng Bangxiong plundered the Yong'an tombs—crimes as base as a thief's cur snarling at Emperor Yao—yet no one was punished.

sentences.zh: 劉正彥附

translations.literal: Liu Zhengyan, appended biography.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Biography of Liu Zhengyan

sentences.zh: 苗傅，上黨人。

translations.literal: Miao Fu, a man of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu was a native of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 大父授，父履。

translations.literal: Grandfather Shou, father Lü.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was named Shou; his father, Lü.

sentences.zh: 授在元豐中爲殿前都指揮使。

translations.literal: Shou in the Yuanfeng era was Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Front Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng reign Shou served as commander of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 康王建元帥府，信德守臣梁揚祖以兵萬人至，傅與張俊、楊沂中、田師中皆隸麾下。

translations.literal: Prince Kang established a marshal's headquarters; Liang Yangzu, defender of Xinde, arrived with ten thousand troops—Fu together with Zhang Jun, Yang Yizhong, and Tian Shizhong all came under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kang raised his field headquarters, Liang Yangzu marched from Xinde with ten thousand men; Miao Fu, along with Zhang Jun, Yang Yizhong, and Tian Shizhong, entered his service.

sentences.zh: 隆祐太后南渡，傅爲統制官，以所部八千人扈衛，駐於杭州。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Longyou crossed south, Fu was a regimental commander; with eight thousand troops of his command he guarded her, garrisoned at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dowager Longyou fled south, Miao Fu, a regimental commander, quartered eight thousand of his men at Hangzhou as her escort.

sentences.zh: 有劉正彥者，不知何許人。

translations.literal: There was one Liu Zhengyan—unknown from what place.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a man named Liu Zhengyan, of uncertain origin.

sentences.zh: 父法，政和間爲熙河路[一四]經略使，死王事。

translations.literal: Father Fa, between the Zhenghe years was Military Commissioner of the Xihe Circuit, died in service to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fa had served as military commissioner of the Xihe frontier during the Zhenghe era and died in the line of duty.

sentences.zh: 正彥由閣門祗候易文資至朝奉大夫，後以事責降。

translations.literal: Zhengyan was transferred from Gate Attendant to civil rank as Submissive Grandee; later he was demoted after being held accountable for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengyan had risen from Gate Attendant to the civil post of Submissive Grandee, only to be stripped of rank and demoted when later held to account for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 會法部曲王淵爲御營都統制，正彥歸之。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Yuan of Fa's retinue became Grand Commander of the Imperial Camp; Zhengyan joined him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yuan, a follower of Fa, was appointed supreme commander of the imperial guard, Zhengyan entered his service.

sentences.zh: 淵以法故，薦正彥於朝，復爲武德大夫、知濠州，擢御營右軍副都統制，淵分精兵三千與之。

translations.literal: Yuan, out of regard for Fa, recommended Zhengyan to the court; he was again made Defender-in-chief Grandee and prefect of Haozhou, promoted to deputy grand commander of the Imperial Camp's Right Army, and Yuan gave him three thousand picked troops.
translations.idiomatic: Out of loyalty to Fa, Wang Yuan put Zhengyan forward at court. Zhengyan was restored as Defender-in-chief Grandee and made prefect of Haozhou, then elevated to deputy commander of the imperial guard's right wing; Wang Yuan detached three thousand elite soldiers to his command.

sentences.zh: 以平丁進功，進武功大夫、威州刺史。

translations.literal: For the merit of pacifying Ding Jin, he was promoted to Martial Achievement Grandee and prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His success in suppressing Ding Jin earned him promotion to Martial Achievement Grandee and appointment as prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，正彥討進，請劉晏偕行。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhengyan campaigned against Jin, he asked Liu Yan to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengyan first marched against Ding Jin, he requested that Liu Yan go with him.

sentences.zh: 晏本嚴陵人，陷遼登第，宣和中率衆來歸。

translations.literal: Yan was originally a man of Yanling; he had fallen into Liao territory and passed the examinations; in the Xuanhe era he led his followers to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan was a native of Yanling who had been taken into Liao lands and there passed the civil examinations; during the Xuanhe reign he returned with his followers to the Song.

sentences.zh: 正彥用晏計易旗幟爲疑兵，遂降進。

translations.literal: Zhengyan used Yan's plan to change flags and banners as a decoy force, and thereby made Jin surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Liu Yan's suggestion, Zhengyan swapped out banners to create a dummy force and tricked Ding Jin into surrendering.

sentences.zh: 晏自通直郎遷朝請郎，正彥恥己賞薄而晏獲峻遷，由是𡙇望，乃散所賜金帛與將士，尋被命從六宮、皇子至杭州。

translations.literal: Yan was moved from Remonstrance and Review Attendant to Court Gentleman for Supplication; Zhengyan was shamed that his own reward was thin while Yan received a steep promotion; thereby he resented it, and distributed the gold and silk he had been granted to the officers and men; soon afterward he was ordered to escort the Six Palaces and the imperial princes to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan vaulted from Remonstrance and Review Attendant to Court Gentleman for Supplication. Liu Zhengyan, bitter that his own reward was modest while Yan won a rapid promotion, grew resentful and gave away the gold and silk he had received to his troops. He was soon ordered to escort the imperial household and princes to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年二月壬戌，高宗從王淵議，由鎮江幸杭州。

translations.literal: On the renxu day of the second month of the third year of Jianyan, Gaozong, following Wang Yuan's proposal, went from Zhenjiang to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, the second month of Jianyan 3 (1129), Emperor Gaozong accepted Wang Yuan's advice and traveled from Zhenjiang to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時諸大將如劉光世、張俊、楊沂中、韓世忠分守要害，扈衛者獨苗傅。

translations.literal: At the time the great generals such as Liu Guangshi, Zhang Jun, Yang Yizhong, and Han Shizhong held key posts separately; only Miao Fu served as escort guard.
translations.idiomatic: The senior commanders—Liu Guangshi, Zhang Jun, Yang Yizhong, and Han Shizhong—were posted at strategic points, leaving only Miao Fu to guard the imperial retinue.

sentences.zh: 先是，王淵裝大船十數，自維揚來杭，杭人相謂曰：「船所載，皆淵平陳通時殺奪富民家財也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Yuan loaded more than ten large boats and came from Weiyang to Hangzhou; the people of Hangzhou said to one another: "What the boats carry is all the wealth of rich families that Yuan killed and plundered when pacifying Chen Tong."
translations.idiomatic: Not long before, Wang Yuan had sailed more than ten heavily laden ships from Weiyang to Hangzhou. Hangzhou locals whispered among themselves: "Every chest on those boats is loot Wang Yuan stole from wealthy families while crushing Chen Tong."

sentences.zh: 內侍省押班康履頗用事，威福由己出；

translations.literal: Kang Lu, Chief Controller of the Inner Service Bureau, wielded considerable power; authority and punishment issued from himself.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Lu, chief controller in the Inner Service Bureau, had grown dangerously influential—rewards and punishments flowed from his hand alone.

sentences.zh: 其徒奪民居，肆爲暴橫。

translations.literal: His followers seized common people's dwellings and wantonly acted with violent arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: His followers seized private homes and terrorized the city with open brutality.

sentences.zh: 傅等恨之，曰：「天子顛沛至此，猶敢爾耶！」

translations.literal: Fu and the others hated this and said: "The Son of Heaven has been driven to such distress, and they still dare act like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu and his men seethed with hatred. "The emperor has been hunted this far," they cried, "and these people still dare behave so!"

sentences.zh: 其党張逵復激怒諸軍曰：「能殺淵及內侍，則人人可富，朝廷豈能徧罪哉！」

translations.literal: His clique member Zhang Kui again incited the armies, saying: "If we can kill Yuan and the inner attendants, then everyone can grow rich—how could the court punish all?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kui, one of their circle, goaded the troops further: "Kill Wang Yuan and the eunuchs, and every man among us gets rich—the court cannot punish us all!"

sentences.zh: 三月辛巳，拜王淵同簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day of the third month, Wang Yuan was appointed Concurrent Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi in the third month, Wang Yuan was named concurrent signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，淵建幸杭州議，內侍實左右之。

translations.literal: At first, when Yuan proposed the journey to Hangzhou, the inner attendants had in fact guided him on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuan had first urged the move to Hangzhou—and eunuchs had been whispering in his ear all along.

sentences.zh: 及淵躐躋樞筦，衆謂薦由內侍。

translations.literal: When Yuan leapt to the head of military administration, the multitude said the recommendation came from inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yuan vaulted into the Bureau of Military Affairs, everyone assumed eunuchs had put him there.

sentences.zh: 傅自負宿將，疾淵驟貴。

translations.literal: Fu prided himself on being a veteran general and resented Yuan's sudden elevation.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu, a seasoned commander proud of his service, loathed Wang Yuan's rapid rise.

sentences.zh: 正彥雖由淵進，淵檄取所予兵，亦怨之。

translations.literal: Although Zhengyan had advanced through Yuan, Yuan issued orders to take back the troops he had given, and he too resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengyan owed his promotion to Wang Yuan, yet when Yuan recalled the soldiers he had assigned him, Zhengyan turned against him as well.

sentences.zh: 於是傅積不能平，與王世脩、張逵、王鈞甫、馬柔吉等謀作亂。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fu's accumulated resentment could not be settled; with Wang Shixiu, Zhang Kui, Wang Junfu, Ma Rouji, and others he plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu's grievances finally boiled over. He joined Wang Shixiu, Zhang Kui, Wang Junfu, Ma Rouji, and others in plotting mutiny.

sentences.zh: 鈞甫等皆燕人，所將號「赤心軍」。

translations.literal: Junfu and the others were all men of Yan; the troops they led were called the "Red-Heart Army."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junfu and his associates were all from Yan; their unit was known as the Red-Heart Army.

sentences.zh: 傅部分既定，乃紿淵以臨安縣有盜，意欲使淵出其兵於外。

translations.literal: Once Fu's dispositions were set, he deceived Yuan by saying there were bandits in Lin'an County, intending to make Yuan send his troops outside.
translations.idiomatic: With his plans in place, Miao Fu lied to Wang Yuan that bandits were raiding Lin'an County, hoping to draw his forces out of the city.

sentences.zh: 康履得黃卷小文書，有兩統制作「田」、「金」字署卷末，田乃苗，金乃劉也。

translations.literal: Kang Lu obtained a small document on yellow paper; two commanders had signed at the end with the characters "Tian" and "Jin"—Tian was Miao, Jin was Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Lu intercepted a scrap of yellow paper bearing two signatures—"Tian" and "Jin"—at the bottom: Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan.

sentences.zh: 於是頗泄賊謀，以告淵，淵伏兵天竺。

translations.literal: Thereupon the rebels' plot was somewhat leaked; he informed Yuan, and Yuan hid troops at Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Enough of the plot leaked out. Kang Lu warned Wang Yuan, who posted ambush troops at Tianzhu.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊黨亦伏兵城北橋下，俟淵退朝，誣以結宦官謀反，正彥手殺淵，以兵圍履第，分捕內官，凡無須者盡殺之，揭淵首，引兵犯闕。

translations.literal: The next day the rebel clique also hid troops beneath the north city bridge; when Yuan left court they falsely charged him with colluding with eunuchs in treason; Zhengyan personally killed Yuan, used troops to surround Lu's residence, split up to capture inner officials, and all who were beardless they killed entirely; they displayed Yuan's head and led troops to storm the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the mutineers too laid an ambush under the north-city bridge. When Wang Yuan left court, they accused him of plotting with eunuchs. Liu Zhengyan killed Wang Yuan with his own hand, surrounded Kang Lu's house, hunted down palace eunuchs—every beardless man was slaughtered—and paraded Wang Yuan's head as they marched on the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 中軍統制吳湛守宮門，潛與傅通，導其黨入奏曰：「苗傅不負國，止爲天下除害。」

translations.literal: Central Army Commander Wu Zhan guarded the palace gate, secretly communicated with Fu, and guided his clique in to memorialize: "Miao Fu does not betray the state; he only removes harm for all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhan, commander of the central army, held the palace gate but was secretly in league with Miao Fu. He admitted the conspirators and announced: "Miao Fu is no traitor—he is ridding the realm of corruption."

sentences.zh: 知杭州康允之聞變，率從官扣閽，請帝御樓，百官皆從。

translations.literal: Prefect of Hangzhou Kang Yunzhi heard of the uprising, led attendant officials to knock at the gate, and requested the emperor mount the tower; all officials followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Hangzhou prefect Kang Yunzhi learned of the coup, he rushed with the imperial staff to the gate and begged the emperor to appear on the balcony. The whole court followed.

sentences.zh: 殿帥王元大呼聖駕來，傅見黃屋，猶山呼而拜。

translations.literal: Palace Guard Commander Wang Yuan shouted that the sacred carriage was coming; Fu saw the yellow canopy and still bowed with the mountain cry.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Guard Commander Wang Yuan announced the emperor's arrival. Miao Fu, sighting the yellow imperial canopy, still prostrated himself with the formal hall cry of homage.

sentences.zh: 帝憑闌呼二賊問故，傅厲聲曰：「陛下信任中官，軍士有功者不賞，私內侍者即得美官。

translations.literal: The emperor leaned on the railing and called to the two rebels to ask the reason; Fu said in a harsh voice: "Your Majesty trusts inner officials; soldiers with merit are not rewarded, while those who favor inner attendants immediately obtain fine offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor leaned over the rail and demanded an explanation. Miao Fu shouted back: "You favor eunuchs! Soldiers who bleed for you go unrewarded, while men who bribe palace attendants win high office overnight.

sentences.zh: 黃潛善、汪伯彥誤國，猶未遠竄。

translations.literal: Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan misled the state, yet they have not been exiled far.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan ruined the country, and still they have not been banished far enough.

sentences.zh: 王淵遇敵不戰，因友康履得除樞密。

translations.literal: Wang Yuan met the enemy and did not fight; through friendship with Kang Lu he was appointed to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuan refused to fight when the enemy appeared, yet through Kang Lu's patronage he won a seat on the Military Affairs Council.

sentences.zh: 臣立功多，止作遙郡團練。

translations.literal: I have achieved much merit, yet am only made distant-district militia training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: I have served with distinction, yet you leave me a remote district militia commissioner.

sentences.zh: 已斬淵首，更乞斬康履、藍珪、曾擇以謝三軍。」

translations.literal: We have already beheaded Yuan; we further beg to behead Kang Lu, Lan Gui, and Zeng Ze to appease the three armies."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuan's head is already taken—we now demand Kang Lu, Lan Gui, and Zeng Ze be executed to satisfy the troops."

sentences.zh: 帝諭以當流海島，可與軍士歸營，且曰：「已除傅承宣使、御營都統制，正彥觀察使、御營副都統制。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed that they should be exiled to sea islands, that the troops could return to camp, and said: "Fu has already been appointed Commissioner-in-chief and Grand Commander of the Imperial Camp; Zhengyan, Observation Commissioner and Deputy Grand Commander of the Imperial Camp."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promised exile to distant islands and told the soldiers to return to barracks. He added: "Miao Fu is now Commissioner-in-chief and supreme commander of the imperial guard; Liu Zhengyan is Observation Commissioner and deputy commander."

sentences.zh: 賊不退。

translations.literal: The rebels did not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers refused to leave.

sentences.zh: 帝問百官計安出，浙西安撫司主管機宜文字時希孟曰：「禍由中官，不悉除之，禍未已也。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the officials where a plan should come from; Shi Ximeng, staff clerk for strategy of the Ji-Xi Pacification Commission, said: "The disaster arises from inner officials; if they are not all removed, the disaster is not yet ended."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to his ministers for counsel. Shi Ximeng, a strategy clerk on the Ji-Xi Pacification Commission staff, answered: "Eunuchs caused this crisis. Until they are purged completely, it will not end."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕左右可無給使耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Can I have no attendants at my side?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Must I have no one left to serve me?"

sentences.zh: 軍器監葉宗諤曰：「陛下何惜康履。」

translations.literal: Ye Zongwu of the Directorate of Military Equipment said: "Why should Your Majesty spare Kang Lu?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye Zongwu of the Armaments Directorate said bluntly: "Your Majesty, why spare Kang Lu?"

sentences.zh: 遂命吳湛捕履，得於清漏閣承塵中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Wu Zhan to capture Lu; he was found in the dust layer of the Clear-Leak Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Wu Zhan to seize Kang Lu. He was found hiding in the rafters of the Clear-Leak Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 傅即樓下腰斬履。

translations.literal: Fu immediately cut Lu in two at the waist below the tower.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu had Kang Lu cut in half at the waist right beneath the balcony.

sentences.zh: 傅猶肆惡言，謂「帝不當即大位，淵聖來歸，何以處也？」

translations.literal: Fu still indulged in vicious speech, saying: "The emperor ought not to have immediately taken the throne—when the Exalted Sage returns, how is he to be placed?"
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu pressed on with threats: "You should never have taken the throne. When the captured emperor returns, where does that leave you?"

sentences.zh: 帝使朱勝非縋樓下曲諭之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Zhu Shengfei down by rope from the tower to persuade him gently.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lowered Zhu Shengfei on a rope to reason with him privately below.

sentences.zh: 傅請隆祐太后同聽政及遣使與金議和。

translations.literal: Fu requested the Empress Dowager Longyou to jointly hear government and to dispatch envoys to negotiate peace with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu demanded that Empress Dowager Longyou rule alongside him and that envoys be sent to negotiate peace with the Jin.

sentences.zh: 帝許諾，即下詔請太后垂簾。

translations.literal: The emperor promised; he immediately issued an edict requesting the empress dowager to hold the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and at once issued an edict inviting the empress dowager to rule from behind the screen.

sentences.zh: 賊聞詔不拜，曰：「自有皇太子可立。」

translations.literal: The rebels heard the edict and did not bow; they said: "There is already an imperial prince who may be established."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels refused to bow when the edict was read. "There is a crown prince ready to be enthroned," they declared.

sentences.zh: 張逵曰：「今日之事，當爲百姓社稷計。」

translations.literal: Zhang Kui said: "Today's affair must be considered for the common people and the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kui argued: "Today's decision must serve the people and the realm."

sentences.zh: 時希孟曰：「宜率百官死社稷，否則從三軍之請。」

translations.literal: Shi Ximeng said: "It is fitting to lead all officials to die for the altars of state; otherwise follow the three armies' request."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ximeng urged: "Better that all officials die defending the throne—otherwise yield to the army's demand."

sentences.zh: 通判杭州事章誼叱之曰：「何可從三軍邪！」

translations.literal: Assistant prefect of Hangzhou Zhang Yi shouted at him: "How can one follow the three armies!"
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou vice-prefect Zhang Yi rebuked him sharply: "We cannot surrender to mutineers!"

sentences.zh: 帝徐謂勝非曰：「朕當退避，須太后命。」

translations.literal: The emperor slowly said to Shengfei: "I ought to withdraw and yield; the empress dowager's command is required."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said quietly to Zhu Shengfei: "I am ready to step aside—but I need the empress dowager's order."

sentences.zh: 勝非謂不可。

translations.literal: Shengfei said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei objected that this must not happen.

sentences.zh: 顏岐曰：「得太后親諭之，則無詞矣。」

translations.literal: Yan Qi said: "If the empress dowager personally instructs them, then they will have no words left."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qi suggested: "Once the empress dowager speaks to them directly, they will have nothing left to say."

sentences.zh: 時寒甚，門無簾幃，帝坐一竹椅。

translations.literal: The weather was very cold; the gate had no curtains or screens; the emperor sat on a single bamboo chair.
translations.idiomatic: The cold was bitter, the gate uncurtained, and the emperor sat on a bare bamboo chair.

sentences.zh: 既請太后，即起立楹側。

translations.literal: After requesting the empress dowager, he immediately stood up beside a pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Having sent for the empress dowager, he rose and stood beside a column.

sentences.zh: 太后御肩輿出立樓前，二賊拜曰：「今日百姓無辜，肝腦塗地，望太后主張。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager rode in a shoulder carriage and came out to stand before the tower; the two rebels bowed and said: "Today the common people are innocent, their livers and brains smeared on the ground—we hope the empress dowager will take charge."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager arrived in a sedan and stood before the balcony. The two rebels bowed: "Innocent people are dying in the streets today. Only Your Majesty can settle this."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「道君皇帝任蔡京、王黼，更祖宗法，童貫起邊釁，所以致金人之禍。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "The Dao-jun Emperor employed Cai Jing and Wang Fu, changed the ancestral laws, and Tong Guan provoked border strife—therefore the disaster of the Jin people was brought about.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager replied: "Emperor Huizong trusted Cai Jing and Wang Fu, abandoned our forefathers' ways, and let Tong Guan provoke war on the frontier—that is how we brought the Jin upon ourselves.

sentences.zh: 今皇帝聖孝，無失德，止爲黃潛善、汪伯彥所誤，已加竄逐，統制獨不知邪？」

translations.literal: Now the emperor is sacredly filial, without loss of virtue; he was only misled by Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan, who have already been exiled and driven off—is the commander alone unaware?"
translations.idiomatic: The present emperor is filial and without fault. Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan misled him, and they have already been banished. Do you commanders not know this?"

sentences.zh: 傅曰：「臣等定議，必欲立皇子。」

translations.literal: Fu said: "We ministers have settled our decision—we must establish the prince."
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu answered: "Our minds are made up. We will install the crown prince."

sentences.zh: 后曰：「今強敵在外，使吾一婦人簾前抱三歲兒，何以令天下？」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "Now the strong foe is outside; if you have me, one woman before the curtain holding a three-year-old child, how am I to command all under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager challenged them: "With powerful enemies at our gates, how can a woman behind a screen clutching a three-year-old child govern the empire?"

sentences.zh: 正彥等號泣固請，因呼其衆曰：「太后既不允，吾當受戮。」

translations.literal: Zhengyan and the others wept and loudly begged, then called to their masses: "Since the empress dowager will not assent, I ought to receive execution."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengyan and his men wept and pleaded insistently, then turned to their followers: "If the empress dowager refuses, let us accept death."

sentences.zh: 遂作解衣狀，后諭止之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they made a show of removing their robes; the empress dowager instructed them to stop.
translations.idiomatic: They began stripping off their armor as if preparing for execution. The empress dowager ordered them to stop.

sentences.zh: 傅曰：「事久不決，恐三軍生變。」

translations.literal: Fu said: "If the affair is long unresolved, I fear the three armies will produce mutiny."
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu warned: "Delay will only provoke the troops to revolt again."

sentences.zh: 顧謂勝非曰：「相公何無一言？」

translations.literal: Turning, he said to Shengfei: "Chancellor, why do you not speak a word?"
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Zhu Shengfei: "Chancellor, have you nothing to say?"

sentences.zh: 勝非不能答。

translations.literal: Shengfei could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei had no reply.

sentences.zh: 適顏岐至自帝前，奏曰：「皇帝令臣奏知太后，已決意從傅請矣，乞太后宣諭。」

translations.literal: Just then Yan Qi came from before the emperor and memorialized: "The emperor ordered me to inform the empress dowager that he has already resolved to follow Fu's request; I beg the empress dowager to announce instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qi hurried over from the emperor's side and reported: "His Majesty has decided to accept Miao Fu's demand. He asks the empress dowager to announce it."

sentences.zh: 后猶不許，傅等語益不遜。

translations.literal: The empress dowager still would not assent; Fu and the others' words grew ever more insolent.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager still refused. Miao Fu and his men grew increasingly abusive.

sentences.zh: 太后還入門，帝遣人奏禪位，勝非泣曰：「臣義當死，乞下詰二凶。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager returned and entered the gate; the emperor sent a man to memorialize abdication; Shengfei wept and said: "This minister by duty ought to die—I beg an edict interrogating the two villains."
translations.idiomatic: As the empress dowager withdrew, the emperor sent word that he would abdicate. Zhu Shengfei wept: "I should die for this shame—issue an edict denouncing those two criminals."

sentences.zh: 帝屏左右語曰：「當爲後圖，事不成，死未晚。」

translations.literal: The emperor dismissed those at his side and said: "We ought to plan for later; if the affair does not succeed, death is not yet late."
translations.idiomatic: Drawing Zhu Shengfei aside, the emperor whispered: "We must plan for recovery. It is not yet time to die."

sentences.zh: 勝非曰：「王鈞甫，賊腹心也，適語臣曰：『二將忠有餘，學不足。』

translations.literal: Shengfei said: "Wang Junfu is the rebels' trusted confidant; just now he told this minister: 'The two generals have excess loyalty but insufficient learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei answered: "Wang Junfu is their inner circle. He just told me: 'Those two generals are loyal enough but not clever enough.

sentences.zh: 此可爲後圖耳。」

translations.literal: This can serve as a plan for later."
translations.idiomatic: That gives us something to work with," Zhu Shengfei said."

sentences.zh: 是日，帝幸顯忠寺。

translations.literal: That day the emperor visited Xianzhong Temple.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the emperor took refuge at Xianzhong Temple.

sentences.zh: 甲申，太后垂簾，降赦，號帝爲睿聖仁孝皇帝，以顯忠寺爲睿聖宮，留內侍十五人，餘悉編置。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the empress dowager held the curtain, issued a general amnesty, styled the emperor as the Sage and Filial Emperor of Sagacious Enlightenment, made Xianzhong Temple the Palace of Sagacious Enlightenment, left fifteen inner attendants, and relocated all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the empress dowager took up regency and proclaimed a general amnesty. The emperor was styled "Sage and Filial Emperor of Sagacious Enlightenment," Xianzhong Temple became his palace, fifteen eunuchs were retained, and the rest were reassigned.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，赦至平江府，張浚知有變，不拜。

translations.literal: On bingxu, when the amnesty reached Pingjiang Prefecture, Zhang Shu learned of the upheaval and did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: When the amnesty reached Pingjiang on bingxu, Zhang Shu learned of the coup and refused to acknowledge it.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，至江寧，制置呂頤浩遺浚書，痛述事變。

translations.literal: On dinghai, arriving at Jiangning, Pacification Commissioner Lu Yihao sent Shu a letter vividly narrating the upheaval.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Jiangning on dinghai, pacification commissioner Lu Yihao wrote Zhang Shu a letter describing the catastrophe in full.

sentences.zh: 浚乃舉兵。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shu mobilized his forces.

sentences.zh: 戊子，御營前軍統制張俊至平江，浚諭以起兵，俊泣奉命。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Front Army Commander of the Imperial Camp Zhang Jun arrived at Pingjiang; Shu instructed him to raise troops; Jun wept and accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the imperial guard commander Zhang Jun reached Pingjiang. Zhang Shu urged him to march; the general wept as he accepted the order.

sentences.zh: 初，勝非奏，垂簾當二臣同對，今屬時艱，乞許獨對。

translations.literal: At first Shengfei memorialized that when the curtain was held two ministers should respond together; now, given the time's hardship, he begged permission to respond alone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei had argued that regency audiences normally required two ministers in attendance, but given the crisis he asked to meet the empress dowager alone.

sentences.zh: 恐賊疑，乃日引其徒一人與俱。

translations.literal: Fearing the rebels' suspicion, each day he brought one of their followers along with him.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid arousing the mutineers' suspicion, he brought one of their men with him to every audience.

sentences.zh: 傅入對，后勞勉之。

translations.literal: When Fu entered for audience, the empress dowager praised and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao Fu came to audience, the empress dowager praised and reassured him.

sentences.zh: 賊喜，無所疑，故臣僚入對，得謀復辟。

translations.literal: The rebels rejoiced and suspected nothing; therefore when ministers entered audience they could plot restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, delighted and unsuspecting, left the court free to plan the emperor's restoration during private audiences.

sentences.zh: 勝非深結王世修，將處以從官，俾通二凶。

translations.literal: Shengfei deeply bonded with Wang Shixiu, intending to place him in a follower's office so he could communicate with the two villains.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei cultivated Wang Shixiu closely, planning to give him a court post so he could serve as a channel to the two ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 傅欲改元，正彥欲遷都建康，太后謂勝非曰：「二事如俱不允，恐賊有他變。」

translations.literal: Fu wished to change the reign era; Zhengyan wished to move the capital to Jiankang; the empress dowager said to Shengfei: "If both matters are not granted, I fear the rebels will have other changes."
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu wanted a new reign title; Liu Zhengyan wanted the capital moved to Jiankang. The empress dowager told Zhu Shengfei: "Refuse both demands and the mutineers may turn violent."

sentences.zh: 己丑，改元明受。

translations.literal: On jichou the reign era was changed to Mingshou.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the era name was changed to Mingshou.

sentences.zh: 張浚遺書二凶，獎其忠義以慰安之。

translations.literal: Zhang Shu sent letters to the two villains, praising their loyalty and righteousness to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shu wrote the two ringleaders flattering letters praising their loyalty to keep them calm.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，百官朝睿聖宮。

translations.literal: On gengyin all officials attended court at the Palace of Sagacious Enlightenment.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the full court assembled at the Palace of Sagacious Enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 以傅爲武當軍節度使。

translations.literal: Fu was made military commissioner of the Wudang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu was appointed military commissioner of the Wudang Army.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，張浚遣進士馮轓赴行在，請帝親總要務。

translations.literal: On xinmao Zhang Shu sent the jinshi degree-holder Feng Fan to the temporary capital, requesting that the emperor personally take charge of vital affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Zhang Shu dispatched Feng Fan, a passed jinshi scholar, to the temporary capital to ask the emperor to resume direct control of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 復抵書馬柔吉、王鈞甫宜早反正，以解天下之惑。

translations.literal: He also sent letters to Ma Rouji and Wang Junfu that they ought early to restore the right order, to dispel the realm's confusion.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Ma Rouji and Wang Junfu urging them to end the coup quickly and clear the confusion gripping the empire.

sentences.zh: 浚既遣轓，即檄諸路，約呂頤浩、劉光世會平江。

translations.literal: After Shu had sent Fan, he immediately issued orders to all circuits, arranging for Lu Yihao and Liu Guangshi to meet at Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Once Feng Fan was dispatched, Zhang Shu circulated orders summoning Lu Yihao and Liu Guangshi to assemble at Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 傅以堂帖趣張浚赴秦州，命趙哲領俊軍，哲不從；

translations.literal: Fu used a bureau note to hurry Zhang Shu to Qinzhou and ordered Zhao Zhe to take command of Jun's army; Zhe did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu sent a bureau summons ordering Zhang Shu to Qinzhou and tried to put Zhao Zhe in charge of Zhang Jun's army; Zhao Zhe refused.

sentences.zh: 改命陳思恭，思恭亦不從。

translations.literal: The appointment was changed to Chen Sigong; Sigong also did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: They replaced him with Chen Sigong, who likewise refused.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以諫議大夫鄭瑴爲御史中丞。

translations.literal: On renchen Remonstrance Grandee Zheng Yao was made Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Remonstrance Grandee Zheng Yao was appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 賊以武功大夫王彥爲御營司統制，瑴面折二凶，彥佯狂，即日致仕。

translations.literal: The rebels made Martial Achievement Grandee Wang Yan commander of the Imperial Camp Bureau; Yao openly rebuked the two villains face to face; Yan feigned madness and that same day retired.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers installed Wang Yan, a Martial Achievement Grandee, as commander of the imperial guard bureau. Zheng Yao openly denounced the two ringleaders to their faces; Wang Yan pretended madness and retired the same day.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，韓世忠引兵至常熟。

translations.literal: On guisi Han Shizhong led troops to Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Han Shizhong marched his army to Changshu.

sentences.zh: 辛道宗謂張浚曰：「賊萬一邀駕入海，何以爲計！」

translations.literal: Xin Daozong said to Zhang Shu: "If by chance the rebels seize the imperial carriage and go to sea, what plan shall we have!"
translations.idiomatic: Xin Daozong warned Zhang Shu: "If the mutineers drag the emperor out to sea, what then?"

sentences.zh: 浚乃聲言防遏海寇，奏道宗爲節制司參議官，措置海船以避賊。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon publicly announced defense against sea bandits, memorialized to make Daozong a planning officer of the Pacification Commission, and arranged sea boats to avoid the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shu publicly claimed he was guarding against sea raiders, appointed Xin Daozong a staff officer on the pacification commission, and gathered ships—cover to move the emperor away from the rebels if needed.

sentences.zh: 甲午，貶曾擇、藍珪于嶺南，傅追斬擇。

translations.literal: On jiawu Zeng Ze and Lan Gui were demoted to Lingnan; Fu pursued and beheaded Ze.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Zeng Ze and Lan Gui were banished to Lingnan; Miao Fu had Ze hunted down and executed.

sentences.zh: 賊欲以所部代禁衛守睿聖宮，又欲邀帝幸徽、越，張澄、勝非曲諭止之。

translations.literal: The rebels wished to replace the palace guard in guarding the Palace of Sagacious Enlightenment, and also wished to invite the emperor to Huizhou and Yuezhou; Zhang Cheng and Shengfei gently persuaded them to stop.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers wanted their own troops to replace the palace guard at the emperor's residence and tried to drag him off to Huizhou and Yuezhou; Zhang Cheng and Zhu Shengfei talked them out of it.

sentences.zh: 馮轓說二凶反正，傅按劍瞋目視轓，正彥解之，曰：「須張侍郎來，乃可。」

translations.literal: Feng Fan persuaded the two villains to restore the right order; Fu grasped his sword and glared at Fan; Zhengyan smoothed matters over and said: "Only when Vice Director Zhang comes will it be possible."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Fan urged the two ringleaders to end the coup. Miao Fu gripped his sword and glared at him. Liu Zhengyan intervened: "Nothing can be settled until Vice Director Zhang arrives."

sentences.zh: 即遣歸朝官趙休與轓共招浚。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched the returned official Zhao Xiu together with Fan to summon Shu.
translations.idiomatic: They then sent Zhao Xiu, a recalled court official, back with Feng Fan to fetch Zhang Shu.

sentences.zh: 乙未，呂頤浩勤王兵至丹陽，劉光世引所部來會。

translations.literal: On yìwěi day, Lü Yihao's troops raised to rescue the sovereign reached Danyang, and Liu Guangshi led his own forces to join them.
translations.idiomatic: On yìwěi day, the relief army Lü Yihao had mustered reached Danyang, where Liu Guangshi marched in with his division to unite with them.

sentences.zh: 丙申，韓世忠兵至平江，即欲進兵。

translations.literal: On bǐngshēn day, Han Shizhong's troops reached Pingjiang and immediately wished to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, bǐngshēn, Han Shizhong's force arrived at Pingjiang and at once pressed to march forward.

sentences.zh: 浚曰：「已遣馮轓甘言誘賊矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Shu said: "I have already dispatched Feng Fan with honeyed words to lure the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shu replied, "I've already sent Feng Fan to soften them with fair promises and draw the rebels out.

sentences.zh: 投鼠忌器，不可太亟。」

translations.literal: When casting at a mouse one fears harming the vessel; one must not act too hastily."
translations.idiomatic: Strike too hard and you may smash what you're trying to protect—we cannot move too quickly."

sentences.zh: 賊遣張彥、王德聲言防淮，德伺彥醉，並其軍，自採石濟江歸劉光世，彥尋爲人所殺。

translations.literal: The rebels sent Zhang Yan and Wang De, declaring they would guard the Huai. De waited until Yan was drunk, absorbed his army, crossed the river from Caishi to rejoin Liu Guangshi; Yan was soon killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dispatched Zhang Yan and Wang De on the pretext of guarding the Huai frontier. Wang De waited until Yan was drunk, seized his command, crossed the Yangtze at Caishi, and rejoined Liu Guangshi; Zhang Yan was murdered shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，浚以世忠兵少，分張俊兵二千益之，發平江。

translations.literal: On wùxū day, because Han Shizhong's troops were few, Zhang Shu detached two thousand men from Zhang Jun's army to augment him, and set out from Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: On wùxū day, finding Han Shizhong too lightly manned, Zhang Shu detached two thousand soldiers from Zhang Jun's command to reinforce him, then marched out of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 馮轓至平江，浚復遣入責賊以大義，諭以禍福，期雖死無悔。

translations.literal: When Feng Fan reached Pingjiang, Zhang Shu again sent him in to rebuke the rebels with the great principle, instruct them on fortune and disaster, and pledge that even death would bring no regret.
translations.idiomatic: After Feng Fan reached Pingjiang, Zhang Shu sent him back into the rebel camp to confront them with duty, warn them of the consequences, and declare he would accept death without regret.

sentences.zh: 傅等初聞浚集兵，未之信，及得浚書，始悟見討。

translations.literal: Fu and the others, when they first heard that Zhang Shu was gathering troops, did not believe it; only when they received Zhang Shu's letter did they realize they were marked for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At first Miao Fu and his confederates refused to believe Zhang Shu was raising an army; the letter in his own hand finally convinced them they were marked for destruction.

sentences.zh: 奏請誅浚以令天下。

translations.literal: They memorialized requesting that Zhang Shu be executed to command the realm.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted a memorial demanding Zhang Shu's execution as a warning to the empire.

sentences.zh: 詔責浚黃州團練副使，郴州安置。

translations.literal: An edict demoted Zhang Shu to Vice Military Training Commissioner of Huang Prefecture and ordered him settled at Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court stripped Zhang Shu of rank, demoting him to vice military training commissioner of Huang Prefecture and banishing him to Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鄭瑴上疏謂浚不當責，密遣所親謝向變姓名告浚宜持重緩進，賊當自遁，浚然之。

translations.literal: Zheng Yao submitted a memorial stating that Zhang Shu should not be punished, and secretly sent his close associate Xie Xiang, who changed his name, to tell Zhang Shu he ought to hold back and advance slowly—the rebels would flee of themselves—and Zhang Shu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yao memorialized that Zhang Shu ought not be punished, and secretly sent his confidant Xie Xiang under an assumed name to urge restraint: advance slowly, and the rebels would collapse on their own. Zhang Shu accepted the counsel.

sentences.zh: 是日，賊遣苗瑀、馬柔吉將赤心隊及王淵舊部曲駐臨平，以拒勤王之師。

translations.literal: That day the rebels sent Miao Yu and Ma Rouji to lead the Red Heart Corps and Wang Yuan's old command to garrison at Linping to resist the troops raised to rescue the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the rebels posted Miao Yu and Ma Rouji at Linping with the Red Heart Corps and Wang Yuan's former troops to block the relief armies.

sentences.zh: 馮轓至臨平，見馬柔吉，同縋入城。

translations.literal: When Feng Fan reached Linping and saw Ma Rouji, they were both lowered by rope into the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Linping, Feng Fan met Ma Rouji, and both men were hauled over the wall into the city by rope.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，與傅等議，傅曰：「爾尚敢來邪？」

translations.literal: The next morning, in council with Fu and the others, Fu said: "You still dare to come?"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, when Feng Fan met with Miao Fu and the rest, Fu snarled, "You still have the nerve to show your face?"

sentences.zh: 欲拘轓。

translations.literal: He wished to detain Fan.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to hold Feng Fan prisoner.

sentences.zh: 浚逆知之，謬爲書遺轓，言客自杭來，知二公于朝廷初無異心，殊悔前書失於輕易。

translations.literal: Zhang Shu learned of this in advance and falsely wrote a letter to Fan, saying a guest from Hangzhou reported that the two lords had from the first borne no disloyal intent toward the court and deeply regretted the earlier letter's rashness.
translations.idiomatic: Forewarned, Zhang Shu forged a letter to Fan claiming a visitor from Hangzhou had sworn the two ringleaders had never meant disloyalty and now bitterly regretted their hasty earlier message.

sentences.zh: 賊得浚遺轓書，大喜，乃釋轓。

translations.literal: When the rebels obtained Zhang Shu's letter to Fan, they were greatly pleased and thereupon released Fan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized Zhang Shu's letter to Fan, rejoiced at the reassurance, and set Feng Fan free.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，浚得謫命，恐將士解體，紿曰：「趣召之命也。」

translations.literal: On rén yín day Zhang Shu received the order of demotion; fearing his officers and soldiers would disband, he deceived them, saying: "It is an urgent summons."
translations.idiomatic: On rén yín day Zhang Shu received his demotion; fearing his army would melt away, he lied that the order was an urgent recall to court.

sentences.zh: 是日，呂頤浩至平江，與浚對泣曰：「事不諧，不過赤族。」

translations.literal: That day Lü Yihao reached Pingjiang; he and Zhang Shu wept facing each other and said: "If matters fail, nothing awaits us but extermination of our clans."
translations.idiomatic: That day Lü Yihao reached Pingjiang. He and Zhang Shu faced each other in tears: "If this fails, our whole houses go to the block."

sentences.zh: 乃命幕客李承造草檄告四方討賊。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered his staff officer Li Chengzao to draft a proclamation announcing to the four quarters the campaign against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered his aide Li Chengzao to draft a proclamation calling the realm to arms against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊聞勤王之兵大集，即呼馮轓、勝非議復辟。

translations.literal: When the rebels heard that the troops raised to rescue the sovereign had massed in great numbers, they immediately summoned Feng Fan and Zhu Shengfei to discuss restoring the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that relief armies were massing in force, the rebels at once called in Feng Fan and Zhu Shengfei to negotiate the emperor's restoration.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，張俊發平江，劉光世繼之。

translations.literal: On guǐmǎo day Zhang Jun set out from Pingjiang, and Liu Guangshi followed.
translations.idiomatic: On guǐmǎo day Zhang Jun marched out of Pingjiang, with Liu Guangshi close behind.

sentences.zh: 賊亦遣兵三千屯湖州小林。

translations.literal: The rebels also sent three thousand troops to garrison at Xiaolin in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels likewise posted three thousand men at Xiaolin in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，頤浩、浚以大兵發平江。

translations.literal: On bǐngwǔ day Yihao and Zhang Shu set out from Pingjiang with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: On bǐngwǔ day Lü Yihao and Zhang Shu led the main force out of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 詔以浚爲知樞密院事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhang Shu Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court restored Zhang Shu as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 丁未，勝非召二凶至都堂議復辟，率百官三上表以請。

translations.literal: On dīngwèi day Zhu Shengfei summoned the two villains to the chief council hall to discuss restoring the throne; leading all the officials he thrice submitted memorials requesting it.
translations.idiomatic: On dīngwèi day Zhu Shengfei convened the two ringleaders at the chief council hall to settle the restoration; the full bureaucracy submitted three successive memorials begging the emperor's return.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊申朔，帝還宮，都人大說。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the first day wùshēn of the month, the emperor returned to the palace, and the people of the capital rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month, wùshēn, the emperor returned to the palace, and the capital erupted in joy.

sentences.zh: 帝御前殿，詔尊太后曰隆祐皇太后，立嗣君爲皇太子。

translations.literal: The emperor took his seat in the front hall; an edict honored the empress dowager as Empress Dowager Longyou and established the heir as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appeared in the front hall and issued edicts elevating the empress dowager to Empress Dowager Longyou and naming the heir crown prince.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，徙傅淮西制置使，正彥副之。

translations.literal: On xīnyǒu day Fu was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Huai West Circuit, with Zhengyan as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On xīnyǒu day Miao Fu was posted as Huai West military commissioner, with Liu Zhengyan as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，詔復建炎號。

translations.literal: On gēngxū day an edict restored the Jianyan reign title.
translations.idiomatic: On gēngxū day the court restored the Jianyan reign era.

sentences.zh: 是日，頤浩、浚軍次臨平，苗翊、馬柔吉以兵阻河。

translations.literal: That day the armies of Yihao and Zhang Shu halted at Linping; Miao Yi and Ma Rouji blocked the river with troops.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Lü Yihao and Zhang Shu encamped at Linping, where Miao Yi and Ma Rouji barred the river with their forces.

sentences.zh: 韓世忠率先鋒力戰，俊、光世乘之，翊敗走。

translations.literal: Han Shizhong's vanguard fought fiercely at the fore; Zhang Jun and Liu Guangshi pressed the advantage, and Yi was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong's vanguard smashed into the enemy line; Zhang Jun and Liu Guangshi piled on, and Miao Yi broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 勤王兵進北關。

translations.literal: The troops raised to rescue the sovereign advanced to the North Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The relief army pushed on to the North Gate.

sentences.zh: 二凶詣都堂，趣得所賜鐵券，引精兵二千，夜開湧金門遁。

translations.literal: The two villains went to the chief council hall, urgently obtained the iron certificates they had been granted, led two thousand picked troops, and at night opened the Yongjin Gate and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The two ringleaders appeared at the chief council hall, seized the iron pardons granted them, mustered two thousand elite troops, and slipped out through the Yongjin Gate by night.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，頤浩、浚引勤王兵入城。

translations.literal: On xīn hài day Yihao and Zhang Shu led the troops raised to rescue the sovereign into the city.
translations.idiomatic: On xīn hài day Lü Yihao and Zhang Shu marched the relief army into the capital.

sentences.zh: 世忠手執王世修以屬吏。

translations.literal: Han Shizhong personally seized Wang Shixiu and handed him over to the officials of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong himself seized Wang Shixiu and turned him over to the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 苗傅犯富陽，統制官喬仲福追擊之。

translations.literal: Miao Fu invaded Fuyang; the regimental commander Qiao Zhongfu pursued and attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu raided Fuyang; regimental commander Qiao Zhongfu gave chase.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，犯桐廬。

translations.literal: On guǐchǒu day he invaded Tonglu.
translations.idiomatic: On guǐchǒu day the rebels struck Tonglu.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，斬吳湛。

translations.literal: On jiǎyín day Wu Zhan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiǎyín day Wu Zhan was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 時希孟編管吉陽軍。

translations.literal: Shi Ximeng was registered and banished to Jiyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ximeng was struck from the rolls and exiled to Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，傅等至白沙渡，所過燔橋以阻官軍。

translations.literal: On bǐngchén day Fu and the others reached Baisha Ford; wherever they passed they burned bridges to obstruct the government army.
translations.idiomatic: On bǐngchén day Miao Fu's band reached Baisha Ford, burning bridges along the route to slow the imperial pursuit.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，犯壽昌縣，黥民充軍。

translations.literal: On dīngsì day they invaded Shouchang County and tattooed the people to fill the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: On dīngsì day they overran Shouchang County and impressed the populace by facial tattoo into military service.

sentences.zh: 庚申，犯衢州，守臣胡唐老拒卻之。

translations.literal: On gēngshēn day they invaded Qu Prefecture; the defending official Hu Tanglao repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: On gēngshēn day they assaulted Qu Prefecture, but the prefect Hu Tanglao drove them back.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，犯常山。

translations.literal: On bǐngyín day they invaded Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: On bǐngyín day they raided Changshan.

sentences.zh: 世忠請任討賊。

translations.literal: Han Shizhong requested to be entrusted with suppressing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong volunteered to lead the campaign against the fugitive rebels.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以世忠爲江、浙制置使，自衢、信追擊賊。

translations.literal: On dīngmǎo day Han Shizhong was made Military Commissioner of Jiang and Zhe, to pursue the rebels from Qu and Xin.
translations.idiomatic: On dīngmǎo day Han Shizhong was appointed Jiang-Zhe military commissioner and ordered to hunt the rebels through Qu and Xin.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，賊犯玉山縣。

translations.literal: On wùchén day the rebels invaded Yushan County.
translations.idiomatic: On wùchén day the rebels struck Yushan County.

sentences.zh: 辛未，賊屯沙溪鎮。

translations.literal: On xīnwèi day the rebels encamped at Shaxi Town.
translations.idiomatic: On xīnwèi day the rebels made camp at Shaxi Town.

sentences.zh: 統制巨師古自江東討賊還，與喬仲福、王德會信州。

translations.literal: The regimental commander Ju Shigu, returning from suppressing rebels in Jiangdong, joined Qiao Zhongfu and Wang De at Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Regimental commander Ju Shigu, marching back from pacifying rebels in Jiangdong, linked up with Qiao Zhongfu and Wang De at Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賊聞之，還屯衢、信間。

translations.literal: When the rebels heard this, they withdrew to encamp between Qu and Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the concentration, the rebels pulled back to the Qu-Xin corridor.

sentences.zh: 五月戊寅朔，世忠發杭州。

translations.literal: On the first day wùyín of the fifth month, Han Shizhong set out from Hang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month, wùyín, Han Shizhong marched out of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，賊党張翼斬鈞甫及柔吉父子首以降，江、浙制置使周望受之以聞。

translations.literal: On gēngchén day the rebel partisan Zhang Yi beheaded Junfu and the heads of Rouji and his father and son to surrender; the Jiang-Zhe Military Commissioner Zhou Wang received them and reported.
translations.idiomatic: On gēngchén day the turncoat Zhang Yi slew Junfu and the Rouji family and sent their heads in surrender; Zhou Wang, Jiang-Zhe military commissioner, received the offer and reported upward.

sentences.zh: 賊寇浦城縣，夾溪而屯，據險設伏，以邀官軍，統制官馬彥溥死之。

translations.literal: The rebels raided Pucheng County, encamping on both banks of a stream, holding the defiles and setting ambushes to intercept the government army; the regimental commander Ma Yanpu died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels struck Pucheng County, lining both banks of a creek, fortifying the heights and laying ambushes to trap the imperial force; regimental commander Ma Yanpu fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 賊乘勝犯中軍，世忠瞋目大呼，揮兵直前，正彥墮馬，生禽之。

translations.literal: The rebels pressed their victory against the central army; Han Shizhong glared and shouted loudly, waved his troops straight forward, Zhengyan fell from his horse and was captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by victory, the rebels charged the center. Han Shizhong glared and roared, drove straight ahead, knocked Liu Zhengyan from his horse, and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 賊將江池殺孟皋、禽苗翊降，衆悉解甲。

translations.literal: The rebel general Jiang Chi killed Meng Gao, captured Miao Yi and surrendered; the masses all laid down their arms.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel officer Jiang Chi killed Meng Gao, seized Miao Yi, and capitulated; the rank and file threw down their weapons.

sentences.zh: 張逵收餘兵入崇安，喬仲福追殺之。

translations.literal: Zhang Kui gathered the remaining troops and entered Chong'an; Qiao Zhongfu pursued and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kui rallied the remnants and fled into Chong'an; Qiao Zhongfu ran him down and killed him.

sentences.zh: 傅棄軍變姓名夜遁建陽，土豪詹標覺之，執送世忠，檻車赴行在。

translations.literal: Fu abandoned his army, changed his name, and fled by night to Jianyang; the local strongman Zhan Biao detected him, seized him and sent him to Han Shizhong, who placed him in a caged cart and sent him to the temporary capital.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu deserted his troops, assumed a false name, and stole away by night toward Jianyang. Local magnate Zhan Biao recognized him, seized him, and delivered him to Han Shizhong, who sent him to the temporary capital in a prison cart.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，詔班師。

translations.literal: On rén yín day an edict ordered withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: On rén yín day the court ordered the armies withdrawn.
