sentences.zh: 秋七月辛巳，世忠軍還，俘傅、正彥以獻，磔于建康市。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on xīnsì day, Han Shizhong's army returned, presenting Fu and Zhengyan as captives; they were dismembered in the market at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On xīnsì day in the seventh month, Han Shizhong returned in triumph with Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan as prisoners; both were torn apart in the Jiankang marketplace.

sentences.zh: 張逵、苗瑀及傅二子俱已前死。

translations.literal: Zhang Kui, Miao Yu, and Fu's two sons had all already died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kui, Miao Yu, and Miao Fu's two sons had already perished before this.

sentences.zh: 詔釋餘黨。

translations.literal: An edict released the remaining partisans.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued an amnesty for the remaining followers.

sentences.zh: 杜充，字公美，相人也。

translations.literal: Du Chong, courtesy name Gongmei, was a man of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chong, styled Gongmei, came from Xiang.

sentences.zh: 喜功名，性殘忍好殺，而短于謀略。

translations.literal: He delighted in fame and achievement; by nature he was cruel, fond of killing, and deficient in strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He hungered for glory, was cruel and bloodthirsty by temperament, and lacked strategic depth.

sentences.zh: 紹聖間，登進士第，累遷考功郎、光祿少卿，出知滄州。

translations.literal: During the Shaosheng era he passed the jinshi examination, was promoted through successive offices to Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Vice Director of the Imperial Household, and went out to serve as prefect of Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shaosheng reign he earned his jinshi degree, rose through the Ministry of Personnel and the Imperial Household, and was posted prefect of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，加集英殿修撰，復知滄州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era he was promoted to Compiler of the Hall for Assembling Elegance and again appointed prefect of Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingkang crisis he was made a compiler of the Hall for Assembling Elegance and returned to Cang Prefecture as prefect.

sentences.zh: 時金人南侵，郡中僑寓皆燕人來歸者，充慮爲敵內應，殺之無噍類。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin were invading south; in the prefecture those lodging as refugees were all people of Yan who had come over to the Song. Chong feared they would serve the enemy as internal collaborators and killed them without leaving a single survivor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin swept south, Cangzhou sheltered many refugees from Yan who had fled to the Song. Du Chong feared they would act as fifth columns and slaughtered them to the last soul.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，進天章閣待制、北京留守，遷樞密直學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan he was promoted to Hanlin Attendant of the Hall of Heavenly Writings and Northern Capital Commandant, and transferred to Direct Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 1 he was made attendant of the Hall of Heavenly Writings and commandant of the Northern Capital, then direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 提刑郭永嘗畫三策以獻充，充不省。

translations.literal: The investigating censor Guo Yong once drew up three stratagems to present to Chong; Chong paid no attention.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Guo Yong once submitted three plans to Du Chong; Du Chong ignored them entirely.

sentences.zh: 永誚之曰：「人有志而無才，好名而無實，驕蹇自用而得聲譽，以此當大任，鮮克有終矣。」

translations.literal: Yong mocked him, saying: "A man with ambition but no talent, who loves reputation but lacks substance, arrogant and self-willed yet winning renown—put such a man in a great charge, and few finish well."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yong mocked him: "Ambitious but untalented, hungry for fame but hollow, arrogant and obstinate yet celebrated—men like that rarely end well in high command."

sentences.zh: 二年，宗澤卒，充代爲留守兼開封尹。

translations.literal: In the second year Zong Ze died; Chong replaced him as commandant and concurrently as magistrate of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, after Zong Ze died, Du Chong succeeded him as Kaifeng commandant and metropolitan magistrate.

sentences.zh: 三年，以戶部尚書兼侍讀召，未至，改資政殿學士，節制淮南、京東西路，依前京城留守，尋知宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was summoned as Minister of Revenue and concurrent Reader-in-Waiting; before he arrived he was changed to Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance, with control over Huainan and the eastern and western circuits of the capital region, continuing as before as capital commandant, and soon made military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled as minister of revenue and imperial reader; before he reached court he was made academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance with authority over Huainan and the capital region, kept on as capital commandant, and soon given the Xuanwu army commission.

sentences.zh: 七月，以同知樞密院召還，至，即拜尚書右僕射、同平章事、御營使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was recalled as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; upon arrival he was immediately appointed Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, Co-Grand Councilor, and Commissioner of the Imperial Camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was recalled as vice commissioner of military affairs; on arrival he was at once made right vice director of works, co-grand councilor, and commissioner of the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 初，宗澤要結豪傑，圖迎二帝。

translations.literal: At the outset Zong Ze had sought to bind bold men together and planned to welcome back the two emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zong Ze had rallied local champions and plotted to recover the two captive emperors.

sentences.zh: 澤卒，充短於撫御，人心疑阻，兩河忠義之士往往皆引去，留守判官宗穎嘗疏其失。

translations.literal: When Ze died, Chong was deficient in winning hearts; men's minds were doubtful and obstructed; loyalists of the two He regions often all withdrew, and the commandant's aide Zong Ying once memorialized listing his failures.
translations.idiomatic: After Zong Ze's death Du Chong proved unable to hold loyalty; morale collapsed across the north, loyalist bands in the two He regions drifted away, and his aide Zong Ying memorialized against his failures.

sentences.zh: 朝廷謂充有威望，可屬大事，呂頤浩、張浚亦薦之，故有是命。

translations.literal: The court considered that Chong possessed prestige and could be entrusted with great affairs; Lü Yihao and Zhang Shu also recommended him, and hence came this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The court believed Du Chong still commanded respect and could bear heavy responsibility; Lü Yihao and Zhang Shu recommended him as well, and so he received the post.

sentences.zh: 時諸路各擁重兵，率驕蹇不用命。

translations.literal: At the time each route held heavy troops in its grasp, and for the most part they were arrogant and insubordinate, refusing orders.
translations.idiomatic: Every circuit then fielded its own heavy armies, and most commanders were proud, unruly, and slow to obey.

sentences.zh: 張俊方白事，謁未入，俊遽前，充怒戮其使，諸將稍稍慴服。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun was just reporting business when his audience had not yet begun; Jun rushed forward, and Chong in anger executed his messenger; the generals gradually came to fear and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Zhang Jun came to report, he pushed ahead before being announced; Du Chong flew into a rage and executed Jun's messenger, and the other generals began to fear him.

sentences.zh: 高宗將幸浙西，命韓世忠屯太平，王𤫉屯常州。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was about to travel to western Zhe, he ordered Han Shizhong to encamp at Taiping and Wang Yan at Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As Gaozong prepared to move into western Zhe, he posted Han Shizhong at Taiping and Wang Yan at Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 以充爲江、淮宣撫使，留建康，使盡護諸將。

translations.literal: Du Chong was made Jiang-Huai Pacification Commissioner, remaining at Jiankang to take full charge of all the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chong was made Jiang-Huai pacification commissioner, left at Jiankang with authority over every field commander.

sentences.zh: 光世、世忠憚充嚴急，不樂屬充。

translations.literal: Guangshi and Shizhong feared Chong's severity and harshness and were displeased at falling under Chong's command.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi and Han Shizhong dreaded Du Chong's harsh rule and resented serving under him.

sentences.zh: 詔移光世江州、世忠常州。

translations.literal: An edict transferred Guangshi to Jiang Prefecture and Shizhong to Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court reassigned Liu Guangshi to Jiangzhou and Han Shizhong to Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 時江、浙倚充爲重，而充日事誅殺，無制敵之方，識者寒心。

translations.literal: At the time Jiang and Zhe relied on Chong as their mainstay, yet Chong daily busied himself with executions and had no plan for checking the enemy; men of insight were chilled at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan and Zhejiang then rested their hopes on Du Chong, yet he spent his days in executions and offered no strategy against the Jin; thoughtful observers grew deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 金人窺江，充遣裨將王民、張超分守諸渡，乘高據岸，以神臂弓射卻之。

translations.literal: When the Jin spied on the river, Chong dispatched the lieutenant generals Wang Min and Zhang Chao to guard the various crossings separately, occupying the heights and holding the banks, using divine-arm crossbows to shoot and repel them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin scouts probed the Yangtze, Du Chong posted Wang Min and Zhang Chao at the ferries, holding the high ground along the bank and driving them back with divine-arm crossbows.

sentences.zh: 金人復逼采石，時以輕舟薄南岸，官軍奮擊，或沉其舟。

translations.literal: The Jin again pressed close to Caishi; at the time they sent light boats close to the south bank, and the government army fought fiercely, sometimes sinking their boats.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin returned and pressed up against Caishi, sending light craft to skim the south bank; the Song fought back fiercely and sank several boats.

sentences.zh: 一日當晝，金人對江列陣而佯退，衆信之，守益懈。

translations.literal: One day at midday the Jin arrayed their battle lines across the river and feigned retreat; the masses believed it, and the defense grew ever more slack.
translations.idiomatic: One afternoon the Jin drew up in battle order across the river and pretended to withdraw; the defenders took the ruse at face value and slackened their guard.

sentences.zh: 敵諜知無備，夜乃乘數十舟橫江直濟，衆不能御，敵遂登岸。

translations.literal: The enemy spies learned there was no preparation; at night they then took several dozen boats to cross the river straight across, and the masses could not resist; the enemy thereupon landed on the shore.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy scouts found the line undefended; that night dozens of boats crossed the Yangtze at a stroke, the defenders could not stop them, and the Jin came ashore.

sentences.zh: 充亟命統制官陳淬盡領岳飛諸裨校合二萬人邀擊于馬家渡，約王𤫉俱进。

translations.literal: Chong urgently ordered the regimental commander Chen Cui to lead all of Yue Fei's lieutenant officers and combine twenty thousand men to intercept at Ma Jia Ford, arranging with Wang Yan to advance together.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chong urgently ordered Chen Cui to gather Yue Fei's officers and twenty thousand men to intercept the Jin at Ma Jia Ford, with Wang Yan pledged to join the attack.

sentences.zh: 敵氣銳甚，淬戰沒，𤫉引兵遁，充軍潰。

translations.literal: The enemy's spirit was extremely sharp; Cui died in battle, Yan led his troops in flight, and Chong's army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin struck with terrible force; Chen Cui was killed, Wang Yan fled with his command, and Du Chong's army disintegrated.

sentences.zh: 金人陷建康，充渡江保真州。

translations.literal: The Jin captured Jiankang; Chong crossed the river to hold Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin took Jiankang; Du Chong crossed the Yangtze and withdrew to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 充嘗痛繩諸將，諸將銜之，伺其敗，衆將甘心焉。

translations.literal: Chong had once bound the generals severely; the generals harbored resentment, watched for his defeat, and all were glad at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chong had long brutalized his officers; they nursed their grudges, watched him fail, and felt nothing but satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 充不敢歸，乃北約泗州劉位、徐州趙立，欲合兵邀敵歸路。

translations.literal: Chong dared not return; he then went north to arrange with Liu Wei of Si Prefecture and Zhao Li of Xu Prefecture, intending to combine armies and intercept the enemy's line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid to face the court, Du Chong turned north and tried to link up with Liu Wei at Sizhou and Zhao Li at Xuzhou to cut the Jin line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 詔遣內侍任源賜親劄激厲，俾爲後圖。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched the inner attendant Ren Yuan to bestow an imperial letter in his own hand to encourage and exhort him, enabling him to plan for the future.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent the palace eunuch Ren Yuan with an autograph letter urging him on and bidding him regroup.

sentences.zh: 源至常州，道阻未得進，募健士先達上意，充詭詞自飭以報源。

translations.literal: When Yuan reached Chang Prefecture the road was blocked and he could not advance; he recruited stalwart men to reach the emperor's intent first; Chong used deceitful words to rebuke himself in reply to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yuan reached Changzhou but could not get through; he hired bold men to carry the emperor's message ahead, while Du Chong answered with self-rebuking lies.

sentences.zh: 充居真州長蘆寺，守臣向子忞勸充由通、泰入浙，欲與偕行，充畜異志，不聽。

translations.literal: Chong resided at Changlu Temple in Zhen Prefecture; the defending official Xiang Zimin urged Chong to enter Zhe by way of Tong and Tai, wishing to travel together; Chong harbored a different intent and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chong lodged at Changlu Temple in Zhenzhou. Prefect Xiang Zimin urged him to cross into Zhe by Tong and Tai and offered to go with him; Du Chong already had other designs and refused.

sentences.zh: 始，京畿提刑淩唐佐在南京，守臣孟庾歸朝，以府事委之，唐佐遂降于金爲所用。

translations.literal: At the outset the capital-region investigating censor Ling Tangzuo was at Nanjing; the defending official Meng Geng returned to court and entrusted the prefectural affairs to him, and Tangzuo thereupon surrendered to the Jin and was employed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, capital-region investigating censor Ling Tangzuo had remained at Nanjing when prefect Meng Geng returned to court and left the city in his hands; Tangzuo then surrendered to the Jin and entered their service.

sentences.zh: 唐佐雅善充，以書招之。

translations.literal: Tangzuo had long been on good terms with Chong and recruited him by letter.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Tangzuo, an old friend of Du Chong, wrote urging him to defect.

sentences.zh: 完顏宗弼復遣人說充曰：「若降，當封以中原，如張邦昌故事。」

translations.literal: Wanyan Zongbi again sent men to persuade Chong, saying: "If you surrender, you will be enfeoffed with the Central Plains, following the precedent of Zhang Bangchang."
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Zongbi sent envoys promising that if Du Chong surrendered he would be made ruler of the Central Plains, as Zhang Bangchang had been.

sentences.zh: 充遂叛降金。

translations.literal: Chong thereupon rebelled and surrendered to the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chong then crossed over and surrendered to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 事聞，高宗謂輔臣曰：「朕待充不薄，何乃至是哉？」

translations.literal: When the matter was heard, Gaozong said to the chief ministers: "We treated Chong not thinly—how could it come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, Gaozong told his ministers, "I treated Du Chong generously—how could he do this?"

sentences.zh: 下制削充爵，徙其子嵩、岩、崐、婿韓汝惟于廣州。

translations.literal: An edict was issued stripping Chong of his rank and banishing his sons Song, Yan, Kun, and his son-in-law Han Ruwei to Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The throne stripped Du Chong of rank and exiled his sons Song, Yan, and Kun and his son-in-law Han Ruwei to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是冬，充至雲中，粘罕薄之，久之，命知相州。

translations.literal: That winter, Chong arrived at Yunzhong; Nianhan looked down on him; after a long while, he was ordered appointed prefect of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Du Chong reached Yunzhong. Nianhan treated him with contempt, but in time appointed him prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 充猜阻肆威，同列多不協。

translations.literal: Chong was suspicious, obstructive, and arbitrary in wielding power; his colleagues mostly did not get along with him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chong was secretive, obstructive, and overbearing; most of his peers refused to work with him.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，其孫自徙所間走歸充，其副胡景山誣充陰通朝廷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, his grandson escaped from exile and returned to Chong; his deputy Hu Jingshan falsely accused Chong of secretly communicating with the court.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 2 his grandson fled banishment to rejoin him, and his deputy Hu Jingshan charged that Du Chong was in secret contact with the Southern Song court.

sentences.zh: 粘罕下充吏，炮掠備至，不服，釋之，因問充曰：「汝欲復歸南朝邪？」

translations.literal: Nianhan handed Chong over to the officials; roasting and plundering torture was applied to the fullest; he did not confess; they released him, and then asked Chong, saying: "Do you wish to return to the Southern Dynasty?"
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan turned Du Chong over to the magistrates, who tortured him with fire and extortion to the limit. He would not confess and was released, whereupon Nianhan asked him, "Do you mean to go back to the Southern Song?"

sentences.zh: 充曰：「元帥敢歸，充不敢也。」

translations.literal: Chong said: "If the Marshal dares return, Chong would not dare."
translations.idiomatic: Du Chong replied, "If Your Excellency dares go back, I certainly do not."

sentences.zh: 粘罕哂之。

translations.literal: Nianhan snickered at him.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan gave a derisive laugh.

sentences.zh: 七年，命充爲燕京三司使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Chong was ordered to serve as Commissioner of the Three Departments in Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 7 he was made Commissioner of the Three Departments at Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 八年，同簽書燕京行台尚書省事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he concurrently signed documents for the Yanjing Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 8 he also served as co-signatory for the Yanjing Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷行台右丞相。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was transferred to Right Grand Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 9 he was promoted to Right Grand Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一年，和議成而充死矣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, peace was concluded and Chong died.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 11 the peace treaty was settled—and Du Chong died.

sentences.zh: 吳曦，信王璘之孫，節度挺之中子。

translations.literal: Wu Xi was the grandson of the Trustworthy Prince Lin, the middle son of Military Commissioner Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi was grandson of the Trustworthy Prince Wu Lin and the second son of the military commissioner Wu Ting.

sentences.zh: 以祖任補右承奉郎。

translations.literal: Through his grandfather's privilege he received appointment as Right Recipient of Favors.
translations.idiomatic: By his grandfather's privilege he entered service as Right Recipient of Favors.

sentences.zh: 淳熙五年，換武德郎，除中郎將，後省言其太驟，改武翼郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunxi, he exchanged to Wude Lang, was appointed Central Court Gentleman-General; the Secretariat said this was too hasty, and he was changed to Wuyi Lang.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 5 he transferred to Wude Lang and was made Central Court Gentleman-General, but the Secretariat protested that the promotion was too rapid and he was reduced to Wuyi Lang.

sentences.zh: 累遷高州刺史。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he rose to Prefect of Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to prefect of Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 紹熙四年，挺卒，起復濠州團練使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxi, Ting died; he was called from mourning to serve as Regimentation Commissioner of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxi 4, when Wu Ting died, Xi was recalled from mourning to serve as regimentation commissioner of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 慶元元年冬，由建康軍馬都統制除知興州兼利西路安撫使。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Qingyuan, from Commandant of Jiankang military horses he was appointed Prefect of Xingzhou concurrently Pacification Commissioner of Lixi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Qingyuan 1 he left his post as Jiankang horse commandant to become prefect of Xingzhou and pacification commissioner of Lixi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 四年，憲聖園陵成，以勞遷武甯軍承宣使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when Empress Dowager Xiaosheng's tomb was completed, he was transferred for merit to Bearer of the title of Martial Tranquility Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingyuan 4, when Empress Xiaosheng's mausoleum was finished, he was rewarded with the honorary title of Martial Tranquility Army Bearer.

sentences.zh: 六年，光宗攢陵成，遷太尉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when Guangzong's provisional tomb was completed, he was transferred to Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingyuan 6, after Guangzong's provisional tomb was completed, he was promoted to Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 會韓侂胄謀開邊，曦潛畜異志，因附侂胄求還蜀。

translations.literal: Just then Han Tuozhou schemed to open the frontier; Xi secretly harbored a different intent; he attached himself to Tuozhou requesting return to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Tuozhou began plotting a frontier war, Wu Xi secretly nursed other ambitions and curried favor with him, asking to be sent back to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 樞密何澹覺其意，力沮之。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor of Military Affairs He Dan perceived his intent and strongly obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor He Dan saw through his design and fought hard to block the appointment.

sentences.zh: 陳自強納曦厚賂，陰贊侂胄，遂命曦興州駐紮御前諸軍都統制，兼知興州、利州西路安撫使。

translations.literal: Chen Ziqiang accepted Xi's lavish bribes and secretly backed Tuozhou; thus Xi was appointed Overall Commander of the Imperial Guard armies stationed at Xingzhou, concurrently Prefect of Xingzhou and Pacification Commissioner of Lizhou West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ziqiang took Wu Xi's heavy bribes and quietly urged Tuozhou on, and Wu Xi was made overall commander of the imperial armies at Xingzhou, with concurrent posts as prefect of Xingzhou and pacification commissioner of Lizhou West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 從政郎朱不棄上侂胄書，謂曦不可主西師，侂胄不報。

translations.literal: Associate Gentleman Zhu Buqi submitted a letter to Tuozhou, saying Xi should not command western armies; Tuozhou did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Buqi, an associate gentleman, wrote to Tuozhou warning that Wu Xi was unfit to command the western armies; Tuozhou ignored him.

sentences.zh: 曦至鎮，譖副都統制王大節，罷之，更不除副帥，而兵權悉歸於曦。

translations.literal: When Xi reached his post, he slandered Deputy Overall Commander Wang Dajie, had him dismissed, thereafter appointed no deputy commander, and all military authority rested with Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Once at his command, Wu Xi denounced his deputy Wang Dajie and had him removed; he never named another second-in-command, and kept every lever of military power in his own hands.

sentences.zh: 開禧二年，朝廷議出師，詔曦爲四川宣撫副使，仍知興州，聽便宜行事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaixi, the court debated dispatching troops; Xi was ordered Sichuan Military Commissioner Deputy, still Prefect of Xingzhou, authorized to act at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaixi 2, as the court debated going to war, Wu Xi was named deputy military commissioner of Sichuan while retaining Xingzhou, with authority to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 自紹興末，王人出總蜀賦，移牒宣司，勢均禮敵。

translations.literal: Since late Shaoxing, Wang Ren had overall charge of Shu tax revenue, exchanged documents with the Military Commissioner's office as equals in power and ritual standing.
translations.idiomatic: Since the late Shaoxing era Wang Ren had overseen Sichuan's finances and dealt with the military commissioner's office as an equal in rank and ceremony.

sentences.zh: 而侂胄以總計隸宣司，副使得節制按劾，而財賦之權又歸於曦。

translations.literal: But Tuozhou placed the chief accountant under the Military Commissioner's office; the deputy commissioner gained authority to oversee and impeach, and fiscal power again returned to Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou then subordinated the chief fiscal officer to the military commission, giving the deputy commissioner power to supervise and investigate—and with that, control of revenue passed back to Wu Xi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，兼陝西、河東招撫使。

translations.literal: Before long, he concurrently served as Commissioner for Pacification of Shaanxi and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was also made commissioner for pacification of Shaanxi and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 曦與從弟晛及徐景望、趙富、米修之、董鎮共爲反謀，陰遣客姚淮源獻關外階、成、和、鳳四州于金，求封爲蜀王。

translations.literal: Xi with his cousin Xi and Xu Jingwang, Zhao Fu, Mi Xiuzhi, and Dong Zhen together plotted rebellion; secretly he sent the client Yao Huaiyuan to offer the four prefectures beyond the passes—Jie, Cheng, He, and Feng—to the Jin, seeking enfeoffment as King of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi, his cousin Wu Xian, and Xu Jingwang, Zhao Fu, Mi Xiuzhi, and Dong Zhen formed a treasonous conspiracy; secretly he sent Yao Huaiyuan to surrender the four border prefectures of Jie, Cheng, He, and Feng to the Jin in exchange for the title King of Shu.

sentences.zh: 侂胄日夜望曦進兵，曦陽爲持重，按兵河池不進，潛爲金人地以困王師，侂胄不之覺。

translations.literal: Tuozhou day and night hoped Xi would advance; Xi pretended to be cautious, held troops at Hechi without advancing, secretly ceding territory to the Jin to hamstring imperial troops; Tuozhou did not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou waited day and night for Wu Xi to march, but Wu Xi feigned caution, kept his army at Hechi, and quietly yielded ground to the Jin to cripple the Song forces—while Tuozhou noticed nothing.

sentences.zh: 會正使程松至，曦不庭參，松不敢詰；

translations.literal: When the chief envoy Cheng Song arrived, Xi did not attend court audience; Song dared not question him;
translations.idiomatic: When chief envoy Cheng Song arrived, Wu Xi refused the formal audience, and Song did not dare press the matter;

sentences.zh: 曦復多摘取松衛兵，松亦不悟。

translations.literal: Xi again took many of Song's guard troops; Song still did not realize.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi also stripped away many of Song's guards, and Song still failed to understand.

sentences.zh: 金人犯西和，王喜、魯翼拒之。

translations.literal: The Jin invaded Xihe; Wang Xi and Lu Yi resisted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked Xihe, Wang Xi and Lu Yi held them off.

sentences.zh: 戰方急，曦傳令退保黑穀，軍遂潰。

translations.literal: Battle was just intense when Xi issued an order to withdraw and hold Black Valley; the army thereupon collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the fighting grew fierce, Wu Xi ordered a retreat to Black Valley, and the army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 乃焚河池，退壁青野原。

translations.literal: He then burned Hechi and withdrew to fortify Qingye Plain.
translations.idiomatic: He burned Hechi and fell back to entrench himself on Qingye Plain.

sentences.zh: 曦時已布腹心于金，將士未之知，猶力戰，敵人竊笑之。

translations.literal: Xi had already planted trusted men with the Jin; officers and soldiers did not know; they still fought fiercely; the enemy secretly laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi had already placed his agents with the Jin, though his troops knew nothing and still fought hard—while the enemy quietly mocked them.

sentences.zh: 曦退壁魚關，招集忠義，厚賜以收衆心。

translations.literal: Xi withdrew to fortify Yu Pass, gathered loyalists, and lavished rewards to win hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi withdrew to Yu Pass, rallied loyal volunteers, and paid out lavish rewards to win the troops over.

sentences.zh: 興元都統制毋思以重兵守大散關，曦因撤驀關之戍，敵由版閘穀繞出思後，思遁。

translations.literal: Xingyuan Overall Commander Mu Si guarded Dasan Pass with heavy troops; Xi consequently withdrew the garrison at Mokan Pass; the enemy went around via Banzhang Valley behind Si's rear; Si fled.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Si, overall commander at Xingyuan, held Dasan Pass with a large force; Wu Xi pulled the garrison from Mokan Pass, and the Jin slipped through Banzhang Valley to get behind him—whereupon Mu Si fled.

sentences.zh: 金遂陷大散關，曦退屯罝口。

translations.literal: The Jin thereupon captured Dasan Pass; Xi withdrew to camp at Zhakou.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin then took Dasan Pass, and Wu Xi fell back to Zhakou.

sentences.zh: 舉人陳國飾投匭上書，言曦必叛，侂胄不省。

translations.literal: Juren Chen Guoshi submitted a letter via the petition box, saying Xi would surely rebel; Tuozhou did not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The degree-holder Chen Guoshi dropped a memorial into the petition box warning that Wu Xi would rebel, but Tuozhou paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 十二月，興州見兩日相摩。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, at Xingzhou two suns were seen grinding together.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month a double sun appeared at Xingzhou, the disks seeming to grind against each other.

sentences.zh: 金遣吳端持詔書、金印至罝口，封曦蜀王，曦密受之。

translations.literal: The Jin sent Wu Duan bearing an imperial edict and gold seal to Zhakou, enfeoffing Xi as King of Shu; Xi secretly accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin dispatched Wu Duan to Zhakou with an edict and a golden seal making Wu Xi King of Shu, and Wu Xi accepted them in secret.

sentences.zh: 李好義敗金人于七方關，曦不上其捷，還興州。

translations.literal: Li Haoyi defeated the Jin at Qifang Pass; Xi did not report his victory and returned to Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Haoyi routed the Jin at Qifang Pass, but Wu Xi suppressed the report of victory and returned to Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 是夜，天赤如血，光燭地如晝。

translations.literal: That night heaven was red as blood; light illuminated the earth as at day.
translations.idiomatic: That night the sky turned blood-red, and the glow lit the ground bright as noon.

sentences.zh: 翌日，曦召幕屬諭意，謂東南失守，車駕幸四明，今宜從權濟事，衆失色。

translations.literal: The next day Xi summoned his staff to state his intent, saying the southeast was lost, the imperial carriage had gone to Siming, and now one should act expediently; all paled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wu Xi called his staff together and declared that the southeast had fallen, the emperor had fled to Siming, and extraordinary measures were now required; everyone turned pale.

sentences.zh: 王翼、楊騤之抗言曰：「如此，則相公八十年忠孝門戶，一朝掃地矣！」

translations.literal: Wang Yi and Yang Xunzhi spoke out in opposition, saying: "If it comes to this, then the Minister's eighty years of loyal household will be swept clean in one morning!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi and Yang Xunzhi protested boldly: "Do this, and eighty years of your family's loyalty and honor will be destroyed in a single day!"

sentences.zh: 曦曰：「吾意已決。」

translations.literal: Xi said: "My mind is already decided."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi replied, "My decision is made."

sentences.zh: 即詣甲仗庫，集兵將官語故，祿禧、褚青、王喜、王大中等皆稱賀聽命。

translations.literal: He then went to the armory, gathered military officers to explain the cause; Lu Xi, Chu Qing, Wang Xi, Wang Zhong, and others all congratulated him and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He went straight to the armory, assembled the officers, and laid out his plan; Lu Xi, Chu Qing, Wang Xi, Wang Zhong, and the rest congratulated him and fell in line.

sentences.zh: 曦北向受印。

translations.literal: Xi faced north and received the seal.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi turned north to receive the Jin seal.

sentences.zh: 遣徐景望爲四川都轉運使、褚青爲左右軍統制，趨益昌，奪總領所倉庫。

translations.literal: He sent Xu Jingwang as Sichuan Chief Transport Commissioner and Chu Qing as Left-Right Army Overall Commander, hastening to Yichang to seize the general headquarters warehouses.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Xu Jingwang as chief transport commissioner of Sichuan and Chu Qing as commander of the left and right armies to rush to Yichang and seize the supply depots.

sentences.zh: 程松聞變，棄興元去。

translations.literal: Cheng Song heard of the revolt, abandoned Xingyuan, and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Song learned of the revolt, he abandoned Xingyuan and fled.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，曦遣將利吉引金兵入鳳州，以四郡付之，表鐵山爲界。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Xi sent the general Li Ji to lead Jin troops into Feng Prefecture, entrusted the four commanderies to them, and set Iron Mountain as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kaixi 3 Wu Xi sent his general Li Ji to bring Jin troops into Fengzhou, handed over the four prefectures, and fixed Iron Mountain as the border.

sentences.zh: 曦乘黃屋左纛，僭王位於興州，即治所爲行宮，稱是月爲元年。

translations.literal: Xi rode the yellow canopy and left banner, usurped the king's position at Xingzhou, made his official residence a provisional palace, and called that month year one.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi took the yellow imperial canopy and left banner, declared himself king at Xingzhou, turned his headquarters into a palace, and proclaimed that month the first year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 使人告其伯母趙氏，趙怒絕之。

translations.literal: He sent men to inform his aunt Zhao; Zhao angrily disowned him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to his aunt, Lady Zhao, who in fury renounced him.

sentences.zh: 叔母劉晝夜號泣，罵不絕口，曦扶出之。

translations.literal: His uncle's wife Liu wailed day and night, cursing without pause; Xi had her carried out.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle's wife, Lady Liu, wept and cursed without cease day and night until Wu Xi had her removed by force.

sentences.zh: 族子僎爲興元統制，見偽檄，色甚不平。

translations.literal: Clansman Pu was Xingyuan overall commander; seeing the false edict, he looked extremely displeased.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Wu Pu, overall commander at Xingyuan, read the usurper's proclamation and could barely contain his anger.

sentences.zh: 曦既僭位，議行削髮左衽之令。

translations.literal: Once Xi had usurped the throne, he discussed implementing orders for shaving hair and wearing the left lapel.
translations.idiomatic: After seizing the throne, Wu Xi debated imposing Jurchen customs—shaved heads and left-lapelled dress.

sentences.zh: 遣董鎮至成都治宮殿，將徙居之。

translations.literal: He sent Dong Zhen to Chengdu to prepare the palace, intending to move his residence there.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Dong Zhen to Chengdu to refurbish the palace, planning to move his court there.

sentences.zh: 曦所統軍七萬並程松軍三萬，分隸十統帥。

translations.literal: Xi's commanded army of seventy thousand together with Cheng Song's army of thirty thousand were divided under ten commanders.
translations.idiomatic: His own seventy thousand troops plus Cheng Song's thirty thousand were reorganized under ten commanders.

sentences.zh: 遣祿祁、房大勳戍萬州，泛舟下嘉陵江，聲言約金人夾攻襄陽。

translations.literal: He sent Lu Qi and Fang Daxun to garrison Wan Prefecture, floated down the Jialing River, and publicly claimed an agreement with the Jin for a pincer attack on Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Lu Qi and Fang Daxun at Wanzhou and sent them down the Jialing by boat, loudly proclaiming a planned joint strike on Xiangyang with the Jin.

sentences.zh: 祁尋至夔，遣兵扼巫山得勝、羅護等砦，以遏王師。

translations.literal: Qi soon reached Kui, sent troops to hold the stockades at Wushan—Desheng, Luohu, and others—to block imperial troops.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi soon reached Kuizhou and sent men to seize the Wushan strongpoints at Desheng, Luohu, and elsewhere, blocking the Song advance.

sentences.zh: 侂胄聞曦反，不知所爲，或勸不如因而封之，侂胄納其說。

translations.literal: Tuozhou heard Xi had rebelled, did not know what to do; some advised that it would be better to enfeoff him thereby; Tuozhou adopted the suggestion.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuozhou learned of the rebellion he was at a loss until someone suggested simply recognizing Wu Xi as a vassal king—advice he accepted.

sentences.zh: 吳晛爲曦謀，宜收用蜀名士以系民心。

translations.literal: Wu Xian advised Xi that he should employ famous Shu scholars to bind popular hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian urged Wu Xi to recruit eminent Sichuan scholars in order to hold the people's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 於是陳鹹自髡其發，史次秦塗其目，楊震仲飲藥卒，王翊、家拱辰皆不受偽命，楊修年、詹久中、家大酉、李道傳、鄧性善、楊泰之悉棄官去。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chen Xian shaved his own hair; Shi Ciqin blinded his eyes; Yang Zhenzhong drank medicine and died; Wang Yi and Jia Gongchen both refused false appointments; Yang Xiunian, Zhan Jiuzhong, Jia Dayou, Li Daochuan, Deng Xingshan, and Yang Taizhi all abandoned office and left.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xian shaved his head in protest; Shi Ciqin gouged out his eyes; Yang Zhenzhong took poison and died; Wang Yi and Jia Gongchen refused the false appointments; and Yang Xiunian, Zhan Jiuzhong, Jia Dayou, Li Daochuan, Deng Xingshan, and Yang Taizhi all resigned and fled.

sentences.zh: 薛九齡謀舉義兵。

translations.literal: Xue Jiuling plotted to raise righteous troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jiuling began planning a loyalist uprising.

sentences.zh: 興州合江倉官楊巨源倡義討逆，未有以發，遂與隨軍轉運安丙共謀誅曦。

translations.literal: Yang Juyuan, warehouse official at Hejiang in Xing Prefecture, advocated righteous suppression of treason but had no means to act; he then jointly plotted with camp transport commissioner An Bing to kill Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Juyuan, a warehouse clerk at Hejiang in Xingzhou, called for armed resistance but lacked the means until he joined the camp transport commissioner An Bing in a plot to assassinate Wu Xi.

sentences.zh: 會李好義與兄好古、李貴等皆有謀，交相結納。

translations.literal: Just then Li Haoyi with his brother Haogu, Li Gui, and others all had plans; they mutually joined together.
translations.idiomatic: Li Haoyi, his brother Li Haogu, Li Gui, and others were already conspiring, and the groups joined forces.

sentences.zh: 二月甲戌夜，漏盡，巨源、好義首率勇敢七十人斧門以入。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu night of the second month, when the water clock ran out, Juyuan and Haoyi first led seventy brave men to axe through the gate and enter.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of jiaxu in the second month, after the watch had ended, Yang Juyuan and Li Haoyi led seventy determined men and hacked their way through the gate.

sentences.zh: 李貴即曦室斬其首，裂其屍。

translations.literal: Li Gui immediately in Xi's chamber cut off his head and tore apart his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui burst into Wu Xi's chamber, struck off his head, and mutilated the body.

sentences.zh: 丙分遣將士收其二子及叔父柄、弟晫、从弟晛、賊党姚淮源、李珪、郭仲、米修之、郭澄等皆誅之。

translations.literal: Bing dispatched officers separately to capture his two sons and his uncle Bing, brother Zhuo, cousin Xian, and rebel partisans Yao Huaiyuan, Li Gui, Guo Zhong, Mi Xiuzhi, Guo Cheng, and others—all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing sent troops to seize Wu Xi's two sons, his uncle Wu Bing, his brother Wu Zhuo, his cousin Wu Xian, and the conspirators Yao Huaiyuan, Li Gui, Guo Zhong, Mi Xiuzhi, and Guo Cheng—all were put to death.

sentences.zh: 時吳端猶臥後閣，亦伏誅。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Duan still lay in the rear pavilion; he too was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Duan was still resting in the rear hall and was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 徐景望、趙富、吳曉、董鎮、郭榮、祿禧等皆在外，遣人就誅之。

translations.literal: Xu Jingwang, Zhao Fu, Wu Xiao, Dong Zhen, Guo Rong, Lu Xi, and others were all outside; he sent men to seek and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingwang, Zhao Fu, Wu Xiao, Dong Zhen, Guo Rong, Lu Xi, and others were away at the time; assassins were sent after each of them.

sentences.zh: 函曦首獻於朝。

translations.literal: They boxed Xi's head and presented it to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi's head was boxed and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔曦妻子處死，親昆弟除名勒停，吳璘子孫並徙出蜀，吳玠子孫免連坐，通主璘祀。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xi's wife and children executed; his close brothers were struck from the rolls and suspended; Wu Lin's descendants were all exiled from Shu; Wu Jie's descendants were exempt from guilt by association and continued to maintain Lin's sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict condemned Wu Xi's wife and children to death, struck his brothers from the rolls and barred them from office, exiled all descendants of Wu Lin from Sichuan, exempted the line of Wu Jie from collective punishment, and ordered that Wu Lin's ancestral rites be maintained.

sentences.zh: 曦敗時年四十六。

translations.literal: When Xi was defeated he was forty-six years old.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi was forty-six when his rebellion collapsed.
